articleTitle: Electron Spectroscopy Studies on Magneto-Optical Media and Plastic Substrate Interface
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The depth-profiles of amorphous TbFeCo films sputtered onto polycarbonate substrate were studied by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Oxidized metals, oxides and hydroxides for example, and adsorbed impurities were found to exist mainly in the vicinity of the film surface and film/ substrate interface.

articleTitle: Permeability of CoNbZr Amorphous Thin Films Over a Wide Frequency Range
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoNbZr amorphous films have attracted the attention of many researchers because of their high saturation magnetization, high permeability, low coercivity, and nearly zero magnetostriction. For these films to be used, one of the important magnetic properties is the behavior of the permeability over a wide frequency range. We have measured the permeability of a square-shaped magnetic film (13 mm × 55 mm) sputtered on a glass substrate from 1 MHz to 400 MHz using a stripline. Over 400 MHz, the permeability of the magnetic film was measured using a ring-shaped sample mounted in a coaxial fixture. The wall motion permeability of CoNbZr amorphous films decreases from 1 kHz to nearly zero at 1 MHz. The rotation permeability is constant to 100 MHz and ferromagnetic resonance is observed near 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Effects on Combustion
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Continuous measurement of combustion temperature and speed in a magnetic field was studied to precisely determine the nature of combustion in a field. When methanol was burned in a magnetic field, combustion speed only decreased to a low value at 0.9 T. Combustion reaction speed is inhibited at 0.9 T, and it seems that effectively the combustion temperature is reduced. Also, there is a tendency to large fluctuations of combustion temperature variation amplitude and frequency in the magnetic field.

articleTitle: Thin Film Media for Hard Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic disk storage devices are normally used as the main on-line files for information processing systems. Particulate disk media have been primarily used for this purpose. In 1982, however, a magnetic disk storage system which employs thin film disk media having an areal recording density of 24 kbits/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was developed. In addition, small hard disk drives mounting thin film disk media 3 ~ 5 inches in diameter are currently being utilized in personal computers and intelligent data terminals. This review summarizes recent developments in this film disk media for longitudinal and perpendicular recording, mainly with respect to the design of read/write operations. The problems to be solved beforehigh areal recording densities and high reliability can be achieved are also considered.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Sputtered (Gd,Tb)-(Fe,Co) Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of Ar pressure on internal stress and magnetic characteristics of various rare-earth transition metal (Gd or Tb)-(Co or Fe) films were studied. Increasing the Ar pressure changed the internal stress of all of the films tested from compressive to tensile. The authors suggest that Ar pressure affects internal stress and fractured the cross-sectional structure because the pressure affects the mean free path of the particles.

articleTitle: Simulation of Spacing between Magnetic Head and Medium of Video Floppy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A simulation of the spacing between a magnetic head and medium has been performed to investigate the spacing characteristics of head shapes used with video floppy disks. In this simulation, the finite element method was used to solve Reynold's equation and the equation of motion for the transformation of the medium. Both equations were discretized simultaneously. The analysis yielded the following results: 1) This method can be used to efficiently obtain a converging solution, despite the non-linearity of the equations. 2) The spacing has a tendency to be constant with respect to protrusions of the head. 3) The effect of a groove on the head surface is the same as that of a narrow track width for the head. 4) For practical use, the groove should have a depth and width of more than 2 μm and 5 μm, respectively.

articleTitle: Application of Stochastic Finite Element Method to the Analysis of Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes application of the stochastic finite element method to a magnetic field analysis. The dimensions or the material constants of a magnetic device are considered as probabilistic space-stochastic processes. When magnetic permeability provides uncertain distribution on the surface or in the body of the magnetic material, the uncertainty can be taken into account. In order to obtain the effect of the deviation, a number of repeated calculations are necessary with the conventional FEM. The present stochastic FEM, however, requires no such repetitions, considerably reducing computing time. The calculated standard deviation makes it possible to evaluate the reliability of magnetic materials or power apparatus.

articleTitle: Ferrite Plating by Means of Thin Film of Reaction Solution; "Thin Liquid-Film Method"
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new method is proposed for ferrite plating to overcome the disadvantages with the conventional ferrite plating based on the rotating disk method and spraying method. The ferrite film is grown in a stainless steel reaction cell, in which the reaction solution forms a "thin (~ 50 μm) liquid film" between a substrate and a cell wall. By intermittently introducing an oxidizing solution, which contains air as an oxidizing reagent, the metal ions (Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, etc) in the "liquid thin film" react into crystalline spinel film on the surface of the substrate. In the new method, oxygen concentration and the flow rate of the solution are much easier to control than in the previous method, and the reaction cell is much simpler too.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Recent developments in perpendicular magnetic recording media are summarized. The conditions for achieving perpendicular recording in a medium are discussed from the viewpoints of crystal structure and orientation, and the microstructure and magnetic properties of the medium. Co-Cr sputtered film, which comprises the mainstream of such media, is described in detail with respect to the above conditions. The reasons why Co-Cr media are preferable to other materials for use as perpendicular recording media are explained. Other candidate materials, as well as future problems related to perpendicular recording media, are also discussed.

articleTitle: A Wide Frequency Planar Inductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A planar inductor previously proposed by the authors, consisting of magnetic layers, insulating layers and a coil, has a finite capacitance between the coil and insulating material, and the resulting L-C resonance limits the operable bandwidth. A new type of planar inductor is proposed, in which the insulating layers are omitted to eliminate the stray capacitance, thereby improving the device frequency characteristics.

articleTitle: Bi-Substituted DyIG Thin Films Prepared by Thermal Decomposition Method for Magneto-Optic Recording Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Highly Bi-substituted DyIG thin films on glass substrates with perpendicular anisotropy, which are candidates for use in magneto-optical recording, have been prepared by a thermal decomposition method. Nitrate solutions were spin-coated on glass substrates, and the resulting films were crystallized by annealing at temperatures between 560 and 660°C. X-ray diffraction studies verified that films were single-phase polycrystalline garnets. Dy substitution resulted in uniaxial anisotropy energies (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>) of as high as 8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Compositional dependences of the saturation magnetostriction constant were measured using the cantilever method. Comparison of the measured and calculated anisotropies revealed that the large K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> values of Dy-substituted films originates in magnetostriction and internal stress. In static recording experiments, written bits about 1.5 μm in diameter were obtained. The Faraday rotation coefficient was 3. 7 deg/μm at a wavelength of 633 nm when the film Bi content was 1.55/formula unit.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy in Amorphous TbCo Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Effects of sputtering conditions on perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in amorphous TbCo films prepared by two target magnetron cosputtering have been studied. The perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of amorphous TbCo films depended strongly on negative substrate bias voltage and Ar gas pressure. TbCo films deposited at zero substrate bias voltage and low Ar gas pressure (2 ~ 5 mtorr) showed a positive uniaxial magnetic anisotropy (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>) of 3 ~ 4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in the range of 13 ~ 31 at% Tb.

articleTitle: Galvanomagnetic Effects in Sm-Co Amorphous Magnetic Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Amorphous magnetic films have unusually large Hall coefficients. We prepared Sm-Co amorphous films with planar or perpendicular magnetization, and studied the galvanomagnetic effect in these films. In this paper, we report on the Sm content dependence of the electrical resistivity ρ, the Hall resistivity ρH, the Hall sensitivity S and the Hall voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">HP-P</sub>. We found that ρH is large because of the large saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and electrical resistivity ρ. The maximum value of ρH is 9.0 μΩ-cm, occuring at 15 at% Sm. We also studied the magnetoresistance of these films.

articleTitle: Formation of Bi-substituted Garnet Films with Perpendicular Magnetization by Thermal Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Conditions for getting perpendicular magnetization were studied for Bi-substituted garnet films fabricated by pyrolysis with iron site substitution amount varied and the kind of rare earth ions varied. Torque measurements of Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> (x = 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2) showed that the film has magnetic easy axis perpendicular to the film plane when x = 0.8 and 1.2. It was also found that K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> results from the stress caused by the difference of thermal expansion coefficient between the film and the substrate.

articleTitle: Transparent Ferromagnetic Films Coexisting with Ferroelectricity of the BiFeO3-PbTiO3 System Fabricated by Reactive RF-Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Reactive rf-sputtered films of solid solution compounds with (BiFeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>(PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> (x = 0 to 1), were examined in an attempt to fabricate transparent ferromagnetic materials which are also ferroelectric above room temperature. The targets were mixed powders of Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, α-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and PbO, in which the first two components were used to synthesize BiFeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> by 1:1 mixing in mol.%, and PbO was added by 5 mol.% with respect to PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> to compensate for the evaporation loss of lead during sputtering. As-grown samples deposited at about 400°C are amorphous but have noticeably large saturation magnetization of 4πMs = 210 G and saturation dielectric polarization of Ps = 0.092 μC/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at room temperature. The samples are turned polycrystalline by post-heat treatment at 700°C for 2 hours in air and 4<o;Ms is increased to about twice the initial value, while Ps is, in most samples, somewhat lower. The samples have a high transmittance in the visible through near-infrared wavelengths. The refractive index n of BiFeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> film is 3.0 at λ = 700 nm.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Artificial Superlattice and Multilayered Films of Magnetic Oxides
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structure and magnetic properties of multilayered films composed of ultra-thin oxide layers are described. Superlattices of CoO/NiO and CoO/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> were prepared by alternating deposition of each on rock salt or sapphire by reactive evaporation. Superlattices of CoO/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> showed an asymmetric magnetic hysteresis at 77 K and at room temperature, induced by magnetic cooling. The Néel temperature of CoO in the superlattices was higher than the bulk value of 18° C. Multilayered films composed of SiO and magnetic oxides were reduced to metal or Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> using hydrogen gas. The reduced films maintained a periodicity similar to that of the original films. Co metal was present in the reduced films in the form of disperse ultrafine particles. Ultrathin Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> layers in reduced films exhibited antiferromagnetism, which was attributed to an unusual iron ion distribution, Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.4</inf>[Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf>Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>]O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Structure of CoCr Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoCr films with thicknesses ranging from 0.014 μm to 0.5 μm were prepared by dc magnetron sputtering onto PET film, using a CoCr alloy (18 wt% Cr) target. Thicker films are characterized by three zones with different magnetic properties. In the first zone, for thicknesses up to 0.03 μm, films have very low coercive forces H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and small saturation magnetizations M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, as well as a poor perpendicular anisotropy. In the second zone, for thicknesses from about 0.03 μm to 0.1 μm, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> vary, both passing through maxima, but the anisotropy field is smaller than that prevailing in the third zone. In this third zone, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> gradually decreases with increasing film thickness, while M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> approaches a constant value and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> reaches its highest constant value. TEM studies showed CoCr films to have a fine columnar structure, with column thicknesses greater than 0.03 μm, and no changes in structure or column diameter were observed for films in the second and third zones. To investigate the effects of the underlayer, various kinds of metal were deposited on the PET film prior to CoCr deposition. Double-layer CoCr films exhibit higher H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> values than single-layer films, and have poor crystalline orientations. SEM observations indicate that CoCr films with a metallic underlayer have smaller grain sizes than do single-layer films.

articleTitle: Reproducing Sensitivity of Single-Pole-Type Head with Co-Zr-Nb/SiO2 Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Effects of domain structures in main pole films on the reproduction sensitivity are investigated for single-pole-type perpendicular magnetic recording heads. The reproduction sensitivity of a single-pole head adopting a Co-Zr-Nb single-layer film becomes unstable and decreases with increases in closure domain sizes, when the track width is made narrow and the anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> is low. On the other hand, for a narrow-track main pole made of Co-Zr-Nb multilayer film with a 50 Å thick SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> intermediate layer, closure domains cannot be observed clearly. Consequently the reproduction sensitivity becomes larger than that of the single-layer main pole, and the reproduced voltage is very stable even for lower H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> and narrower track widths.

articleTitle: Thin Film Head for Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A single-pole thin film head with various parameters, in combination with rigid disks for perpendicular recording, is described. The head was designed by numerical analysis of the head magnetic field before actual fabrication. An amorphous CoZr thin film was prepared for use as the main pole. Compared with Permalloy, this film had a higher saturation magnetization (16000 G) and higher permeability (5000). Heads were then fabricated with an amorphous CoZr main pole, varying the main pole thickness T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> and the main pole depth D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>. The recording characteristics were evaluated in combination with CoCr double-layer rigid disks. To attain high recording densities, both the main pole thickness T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> and the CoCr layer thickness δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cocr</sub> must be made thin. A half-amplitude recording density D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> of 70 kFRPI was achieved using a head with a 0.2 μm pole thickness and a disk with a 0.14 μm CoCr layer thickness. The main pole depth D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> had less of an influence on the recording characteristics, meaning a larger tolerance during head manufacture.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Si-Al Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-Si (0 - 16 wt% Si) and Fe-Si-Al (3 - 14 wt% Si, 0 8 wt% Al, bal Fe) alloy films were prepared by the DC sputtering technique. In Fe-Si films, the equilibrium phase expected from the phase diagram was obtained under sputtering conditions of P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</sub> = 40 mTorr and V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub> = 3.5 kV, while the disordered α-phase was realized as a non-equilibrium phase up to about 16 wt% Si under the different sputtering conditions P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</sub> = 40 mTorr and V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub> = 2.0 kV. The concentration dependence of the magnetostriction λ for Fe-Si films sputtered at V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub> = 3.5 kV was found to be nearly the same as that of bulk crystals. However, for Fe-Si films consisting of the α-phase, the sign of λ remains positive up to about 16 wt% Si. Concentration corresponding to zero magnetostriction, λ = 0, determined for Fe-Si-Al films was found to be different from that of bulk crystals, and also different from that of the evaporated films reported by Kadono et al. Comparing the concentration dependence of λ with that of magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> , determined by the present authors, it is proposed that films with soft magnetic properties, such as those of Sendust alloy, can best be realized in the Fe-rich concentration portion.

articleTitle: Effects of Core Characteristics on Detection Performances in Zero Flux Type Magnetic Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To verify the lack of dependence of a proposed zero flux type magnetic sensor on the material and shape of the core used, the authors constructed sensors using amorphous and supermalloy ribbons, and studied the detection characteristics. Detection levels were found to be unaffected by the type of ribbon core used and by the core shape, and an accuracy to about 0.02% (5 kA/m full scale) was achieved.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties of PtMnSb Films Prepared by RF Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: PtMnSb Heusler alloy films were prepared by RF magnetron sputtering from mosaic targets. Films with a polar Kerr rotation and a Clb-PtMnSb (111) diffraction peak were obtained on glass substrates at room temperature. The compositions of these films were in the range 19 ⩽ x 32, 35 ⩽ y ⩽ 46 and 28 ⩽ z ⩽ 38 for Pt<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> (x + y + z = 100). During DC bias sputtering, the Sb and Mn contents were selectively decreased by increasing the DC bias voltage. For film deposited at 400°C on a glass substrate, the polar Kerr rotation was found to be 1.18° on the glass side when an external 7 kOe dc magnetic field was applied perpendicularly. SEM observations revealed a columnar microstructure, and a perpendicular component of magnetization was detected using a VSM. However, this component was not strong enough to cancel the demagnetizing field.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of TbFeCo Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relationship between the magneto-optical characteristics and the medium noise of TbFeCo films is studied. The M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> changes with temperature in Fe-rich and Tb-rich films differ markedly. Magnetic inversions occurred at high temperatures in films with a large M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, causing a demagnetizing field which left blank sections in the recorded bits and increased the playback noise. At normal temperatures, Tb-rich films have a small M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> and, as a result, less modulation noise.

articleTitle: Influence of Substrate Heating on Properties of Tb-Fe Film Prepared by Vacuum Evaporation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The influence of a temperature gradient during film growth on the magnetic characteristics of Tb-Fe films was studied. Two substrates were positioned in the vacuum chamber with one heated from below the substrate and the other heated from above by infrared radiation from a nichrome heater. This produced films with exactly the same composition, but with opposite in-plane direction temperature gradients. Tb-Fe film deposited on the substrate heated from below had a higher H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub> value than that deposited on the substrate heated from above. Also, the rectangularity of the film heated from above was far better.

articleTitle: Preparation and Characteristics of Co-Cr Films by EP Magnetron Co-sputtering Technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Experimental results are given on high-rate low-temperature deposition of Co-Cr films using an exposed pole (EP) magnetron simultaneous sputtering system developed by the authors for deposition of ferromagnetic binary alloy films. A composite target is prepared consisting of a Co washer, a Cr cylinder, and a Co disk; the performance of the sputtering system is examined and the film quality evaluated. The results are as follows: 1) the maximum deposition rate was as high as 0.18 μm/min for 7.6 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of input power; 2) the deposition rate was higher for lower sputtering gas pressures; 3) the substrate temperature was as low as 100°C for 7.6 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> input power; 4) the C-axis of the deposited Co-Cr films was oriented perpendicular to the film plane, with Δθ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> = 8 to 13°; and 5) perpendicular magnetic anisotropy films were obtained when the film M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> = 300 to 800 emu/cc and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 250 to 350 Oe. Thus it is concluded that EP magnetron simultaneous sputtering is very useful for the deposition of Co-Cr films.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties of Substituted Pt-Mn-Sb Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of substituting a fourth element in the Pt sites and Mn sites on the magneto-optical effect of PtMnSb films was investigated. The Mn sites were much more difficult to substitute than the Pt sites. Films with Co, Ni and Cu substituted for Pt had wavelength peaks with respect to polar Kerr rotation at longer wavelengths than that of the PtMnSb film, which seems to be because the band gap at the Fermi level with respect to the minority spin is narrower than in the PtMnSb film. The wavelength peaks for samples with Cr and Fe substituted for Mn was at lower wavelengths than the PtMnSb film.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of FeCr Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structure and magnetic properties of FeCr sputtered films were studied, and the conditions for perpendicular magnetic anisotropy investigated. Results indicated that films sputtered at an input power of 200 W were bcc, but at lower input powers a σ phase appeared, and films had a perpendicular anisotropy, possibly due to an observed columnar microstructure. When a focusing magnetic field was applied during sputtering, there was less bcc phase material and more of the σ phase.

articleTitle: 0.8 μm Range Optical Isolator Using LPE Garnet Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: (BiGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(FeAlGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> and Ca-doped (BiGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(FeAlGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> garnet thin films were subjected to reducing treatment to decrease the optical absorption loss and increase the figure of merit. These materials were investigated for use as the media in 0.8 μm isolators. The absorption loss α decreased after reduction irrespective of whether Ca doping was used or not, but the film with the lowest (220 dB/cm) was doped with Ca and grown at a low supercooling temperature. The figure of merit |θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>|/α reached a maximum of 30 deg/dB, and that is an excellent result. Corresponding thick films were subjected to reduction processing at 300°C, but the film absorption loss did not change, and after processing at a temperature of over 345°C, cracks appeared on the film surfaces and Fe was deposited.

articleTitle: On Flux Reversal in Amorphous-Core Multivibrator Bridge Circuits for Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Amorphous-core multivibrator bridge circuit systems were studied in single-core and in double-core systems. When the length of the amorphous wire is varied in the range 80 mm to 10 mm, the one-core system detection sensitivity showed small variation in the range 8.5 mV/Oe to 7 mV/Oe, while in the two-core case the sensitivity was high and the variation was 110 mV/Oe to 22 mV/Oe. Zero drift at amorphous wire length of 10 mm is very marked in the one-core system, but magnetic annealing results in stability being reached within 80 min after the power is turned on. In the two-core case stability is reached with 10 min after power is supplied.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Iron Nitride Thin Films with High Corrosion Resistance
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An ion and vapor deposition (IVD), method was used to fabricate iron nitride films for use as evaporated tape media, and their film properties evaluated. In the IVD process, iron was evaporated onto a substrate that was simultaneously bombarded by nitrogen ions. The ion current density J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ion</sub> was varied to investigate its effect on the deposited film. Increasing J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ion</sub> led to formation of ε-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>~<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N over α-Fe, and to lower saturation magnetization and higher coercivity and squareness ratio. Iron nitride film samples showed no changes either in appearance or in magnetic properties even after exposure to a 5 percent saline solution for 300 h.

articleTitle: Preparation of Magnetostrictive Layers by Wire Explosion Spraying and its Application to Torque Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetostrictive film with high adhesion coated onto a shaft surface by the wire explosion spraying method was studied for applications to noncontact torque sensors. A two-core type magnetic multivibrator was constructed from magnetostrictive film produced by exploding 10 layers of Fe and Ni wire alternately for a composition close to Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>. Torque output characteristics when the current and voltage were varied had very clean linearity.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy of Co Thin Films Prepared by Oblique Incidence
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To investigate exchange interactions between metallic cobalt and CoO, the authors formed cobalt thin films oxidized to varying degrees, by oblique (65°) evaporation onto polyimide films, and studied the magnetic and other properties as functions of x = (metallic cobalt mass)/(total cobalt mass). The coercivity increased with x in all cases, and the temperature dependence of the uniaxial anisotropy constant K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> was similar for all but the most heavily oxidized sample, which also showed a maximum in rotational hysteresis loss W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RH</inf> at 280 K. At the Neél point of CoO is 293 K, considerable amounts of CoO are thought to be present in the film, interacting with matallic Co.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Grain Structure in Rapidly Quenched Fe-Al Alloy Ribbons
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The grain structure of rapidly quenched 16% Al-Fe alloy ribbon after annealing under different vacuum pressures, and the resulting changes in magnetic properties were studied. When annealing is performed the grains grow rapidly to sizes anywhere from 150 to 400 times their previous size. At 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> torr it appears that some of the (110) planes are mixed up with the (100) planes, though the (110) planes increase again at 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> torr, and finally at 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> torr (100) planes appear over the entire surface.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Level and Angle Detector Using Magnetic Fluid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The static operating characteristics of a new type of levelness and orientation sensor, using magnetic fluid and employing the principle of operation of differential transformer sensors, are described. Three output voltages from a single sensor unit enable accurate detection of the sensor angles of orientation within the horizontal and vertical planes over wide ranges.

articleTitle: Process of Magnetization Reversal in a Spot Heated by Pulsed Laser Beam
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The process of magnetization reversal in a bit written by a light beam was observed using a micro-Kerr effect measurement technique. Pulsed laser light (of wave-length 830 nm), combined with a synchronized, sinusoidally oscillating bias magnetic field, caused repeated writing and erasing of a bit. By monitoring cw laser light (633 nm) focused on the bit, the change in the Rerr rotation angle due to the rise in temperature was measured. Samples used were amorphous rare-earth--transition-metal (RE-TM) thin films (TbFeCo) sputtered onto glass substrates. For TM-rich films, domains in spots irradiated by laser light in a zero bias magnetic field tend to include magnetic reversal regions; for RE-rich films, in contrast, there is a single stable domain.

articleTitle: Thickness Dependence of Effective Composition for Amorphous TbFe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An attempt is made to explain the deviation to the Fe-rich side of the ``effective'' composition of RF sputtered, amorphous TbFe films. The results indicate that the effective composition apparently varies as a function of film thickness, and this cannot be explained using the present model. A thin boundary-layer model is proposed which assumes: 1) these layers are formed at both the film-substrate and film-air boundaries; 2) this layer thickness is independent of the total film thickness; and 3) there are exchange couplings between the boundary layer and the middle layer.

articleTitle: Film Fabrication of Solid Solution of BiFeO3-PbTiO3 by RF-Reactive Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic characteristics of solid solution films (BiFeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) having both ferromagnetic and ferroelectric characteristics and produced by RF-reactive sputtering are discussed. All samples had a high transmittance in the visible to near-infrared wavelengths with a cut-off wavelength of 410 nm and a refractive index of approximately 2.4 at 900 nm. The spontaneous magnetization 4πMs of these films was 550 G, which is noticeably larger than that of bulk and comparable to that of magnetic garnets and orthoferrites. This spontaneous magnetization decreases with increases in PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, and can be effectively doubled through post-heat treatment regardless of the PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> concentration.

articleTitle: R/W Experiment Using High-Speed Flexible Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of EuO Thin Films Doped with Transition Metal
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: EuO films were doped with Co, Ag, or Au and their characteristics studied. These results were then compared with EuO films containing either additional Fe or Eu. It was found that films containing a transition metal had a higher Curie temperature than those containing additional Eu, and the magnetization of films doped with Ag or Fe had similar temperature dependence (a nearly linear decrease at T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sup>). Two Curie temperatures were observed in films doped with Co or Au, indicating two magnetic phases.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optic Properties of PtMnSb Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: PtMnSb thin films were prepared by evaporation and the influence of annealing conditions on magnetic and magneto-optic characteristics was investigated. The saturation magnetization of films in which C2-phase was formed was found to be considerably lower than that of film without it. Measurement of the Kerr rotation showed that the formation of C2-phase also had a deleterious effect on the magneto-optic effect.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties of (GdBi)3(FeAl)5O12 Bulk Single Crystals and Their Application to a 1.3 μm Optical Isolator
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A compact optical isolator has been developed for use at a wavelength of 1.3 μm, using a Bi-substituted gadolinium iron garnet (Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>) single crystal as a Faraday rotator. The optical isolator features a 0.35 dB insertion loss, 34 dB backward loss, and approximately 33.6 dB isolation ratio at 1.3 μm. The insertion loss and the magneto-optical figure of merit in Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1·8</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1·2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> at 1.3 μ are about 0.025 dB and 3000 deg/dB, respectively. The temperature and magnetic field dependences of the Faraday rotation and the optical absorption have been measured for Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-y</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> single crystals, grown by an improved flux method in which Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> is used as a flux. The saturation field of the Faraday rotation decreases with Al substitution. The magneto-optical figure of merit of the Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> absorption region at about 0.9 μm was approximately independent of the Al content for y ≪ 0.5. The Faraday rotation in Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (0.85 ≪ x ≪ 1.2) changes by about 7.5%/50°C as the temperature rises above 25°C.

articleTitle: Co-Cr Perpendicular Anisotropy Film Deposited by Evaporation with Ion Bombardment
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Changes in CoCr films induced by argon ion bombardment during film deposition by evaporation were studied. The film magnetic properties and X-ray rocking curve widths indicated that ion bombardment during deposition results in greater film uniformity, with larger crystal grains, better crystal orientation and less Cr segregation. This is probably because ion bombardment promotes atomic diffusion in films, thereby reducing grain boundaries and other lattice defects.

articleTitle: A Closed-Type Planar Inductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A planar inductor with a closed magnetic circuit structure is proposed. Whereas previous devices constructed by the authors consisted of a coil with magnetic layers above and below, in the present device the coil is surrounded by magnetic material on all four sides, for an increase in inductance from 100 nH to 200 nH. However, the bandwidth falls as a result, from 500 MHz to about 250 MHz. The increase in L is thought to be due primarily to the decrease in reluctance accompanying the addition of magnetic layers.

articleTitle: Automatic Measurement of Preisach Distributions in Soft Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The mathematical formalization of Preisach distribution was studied. A peak was observed with its center on the line h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> = h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> (45°) in the Preisach distributions of a non-oriented silicon steel plate S-10 and a grain-oriented silicon steel plate G-7. In the neighborhood of the main peak a valley with negative distribution value can be seen and adjacent to it is a ridge of positive distribution values. This result is due to the fact that magnetization reversal is more difficult in minor loops with larger returning magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Relation between Groove Shape and Signal Quality in Magneto-Optical Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between groove profile and signal quality in magneto-optical disks was investigated theoretically and experimentally. First, the static characteristics of disks were measured using a micro-magneto-optical effect measurement apparatus. The Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>), reflectivity (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>) and coercive force in grooves 0.65 to 0.91 μm wide and 15 to 87 nm deep were similar to the values for the plane surface, except for a reduction in R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> due to groove diffraction effects. Then the carrier-to-noise ratio was examined using a magneto-optical disk drive, and the results compared with theoretical values. A decreased groove depth and increased width yielded good signal quality. As a result, high-quality magneto-optical signals in excess of 60 dB were obtained from a magneto-optical disk with grooves of depth 15 nm and width 0.8 μm, and with a four-layer structure medium consisting of A1N, GdTbFe, and Al.

articleTitle: Syntheses of Amorphous Gd-Co Sputtered Films with Anisotropy Modulated Superstructure
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It was experimentally confirmed that when selective resputtering is performed only the atoms very near the surface layer are sputtered, agreeing well with theoretical predictions and computer calculations. A film with deposition film thickness t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> greater than composition change threshold thickness t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> was found to be compositionally modulated with change in composition of about a few percent. The authors propose to call this new type of magnetic film an anisotropic modulated superstructure film.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Composition Modulated Co/Cu, Fe/Cu Multilayered Films Prepared by Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structure, magnetic properties, polar Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>), and Mössbauer effect of Fe/Cu and Co/Cu system compositionally modulated multilayered films were studied. No satellite peak was found in the Fe/Cu film X-ray diffraction pattern, but a clear satellite peak was observed in that of the Co/Cu system multilayered film, revealing the difference between the structures of the Fe/Cu and Co/Cu multilayered films. A new θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> peak was observed at λ = 560 nm in the multilayered films with thick composition modulation period. The appearance of the new θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> peak at this wavelength suggests the possibility of a new electron transition, because no multiple reflection was observed in the neighborhood of 560 nm.

articleTitle: Single Crystal Growth and Magneto-Optical Properties of Bi, Al-Substituted Magnetic Garnets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Al was substituted for the iron in the garnet in Bi-substituted magnetic garnet single crystals in an attempt to reduce saturation magnetization and absorption loss. The Bi-, Al-substituted magnetic garnet showed an approximately 20 percent drop in absorption in the neighborhood of 0.8 μm wavelength with no loss in figure of merit because η<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> decreased also. Faraday rotation angle measurements established that the saturation magnetism of the Al-substituted crystal was less than half that of the non-substituted crystal. It was also found that as the amount of Bi substituted increases, the compensating temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">comp</sub>) decreases, while T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">comp</sub> increases as the amount of Al substituted is increased. The results showed conclusively that Bi-, Al-substituted garnet is a material with superb magneto-optical properties, with low saturation magnetization and low absorption loss.

articleTitle: Crystalline Orientation and Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy of Iron Oxide Thin Films Deposited by Target Facing Type Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Opposed-target sputtering is employed to produce Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> single-phase films with (111) orientation on glass substrates and ZnO-coated silicon wafers. The magnetostriction values of these films were larger than those of randomly oriented films, which caused the film to have a large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. Low pressure during sputtering improved the (111) orientation, but also increased the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. Attempts to make (111) oriented films on A1 substrates failed, but those made on the ZnO-coated silicon wafers showed epitaxial growth and good reproducibility.

articleTitle: Analysis of Residual Flux Distribution and Consideration of Demagnetizing Conditions of Mild Steel
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In general, residual flux density produces a detrimental effect on a measurement instrument. This report studies the following issues: (1) Analysis of residual flux distribution by the finite element method, taking hysteresis into account. (2) Demagnetizing conditions of mild steel and the demagnetizing method. The demagnetizing conditions and method were confirmed experimentally and the following experiments on demagnetization were made: (a) gradient, (b) frequency, and (c) magnitude.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Perpendicular Magnetic NdFeCo Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The perpendicular magnetic anisotropy constant (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>) of Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x films reaches a maximum of 1 × 10<sup>7</sup> erg/cc at approximately x = 40. The Kerr rotation angle (γ<sub>K</sub>) remains at approximately 0.3° with little variation as x changes. For NdFeCo films perpendicularly magnetized, the coercive force H<sub>c</sub> increased with the Co content. The temperature dependence of K<sub>u</sub> in NdFeCo films was similar to that of NdFe films. The Curie temperature (T<sub>c</sub>) of Nd<sub>40</sub>[Fe<sub>1-y</sub>Co<sub>y</sub>]<sub>60</sub> increased from 400 K at y = 0 to 503 K at y = 0.25.</sub>

articleTitle: Control of Thickness Dependence of Perpendicular Coercivity on Electroless Co-Ni-Re-P Alloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Electroless Co alloy films for use as perpendicular magnetic recording media were investigated with respect to the thickness dependence of their magnetic properties. The read/write characteristics, especially the dependence of the overwrite on the recording density, were very different for Co-Ni-Re-Mn-P films and Co-Ni-Re-P films. Since those films displayed different thickness dependences of perpendicular coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub>), efforts were made to control the thickness dependence of the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub>) of Co-Ni-Re-P alloy films. The thickness dependence of the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub>) of Co-Ni-Re-P alloy films can be easily controlled by adjusting the sodium malonate concentration in the plating bath. When films are very thin, such as 0.1 μm thick, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub>) value and degree of c-axis orientation increased with increasing sodium malonate concentration. However, when the film thickness was increased to 0.5 μm, these properties were nearly the same for different sodium malonate concentrations.

articleTitle: Read/Write Characteristics of Sputtered Garnet Optical Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The read/write characteristics of sputtered garnet magneto-optical disks are described. Polycrystaline films are grown on a glass substrate. In majority of the noise was found to come from the grain boundary. A good film was obtained under optimal sputtering conditions, with a carrier to noise ratio (CNR) of 45 dB. On a GGG substrate, an epitaxial film was obtained. Its CNR was 52 dB. No great improvement over a glass substrate was obtained. It seems that crystal defects are the cause of the noise.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties of PtMnSb Films Prepared by RF Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: PtMnSb films on room-temperature and heated substrates were produced. The PtMnSb films made on room temperature substrates had a maximum Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) of 0.41°, but the θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> of films made on heated substrates reached 1.18° at T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub> = 400°C. Films produced at T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub> = 400°C had a columnar structure with a large perpendicular magnetization component, while those made at T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub> = 200°C had only an in plane magnetization component.

articleTitle: Thin Film Head for Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Thin film heads for perpendicular recording were fabricated, with a main pole of Co-Zr-Nb and auxiliary pole of Permalloy, and their performances compared with those of unilateral bulk-type heads. When recording at 1.7 kFCI, the thin film heads yielded outputs twice as high as bulk heads at the same recording current. According to FEM analyses, this is because from 25 to 50 percent of the magnetic flux passing through the pole tip is linked with the coil, versus only about 15 percent for bulk heads. If the auxiliary pole thickness, auxiliary pole tip position and other factors are optimized, further improvements in sensitivity are possible.

articleTitle: Characteristic Test of Static Power Transmission on the Face-Type Permanent Magnet Torque Coupling
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A characteristic test of the face-type magnetic coupling static power transmission system was performed to obtain basic data on a permanent magnet torque coupling. It was found that facing poles and adjacent poles have to be unlike for maximum transmission torque. It was easy to determine the relation between the phase angle after pull-out and the transmission torque in this static test, something which is very difficult in a dynamic test.

articleTitle: Magnetic Readout Head Using Induced RF Permeability Variation in Ni-Fe Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A novel principle of magnetic readout is proposed which can extract a high-quality output from high-density recorded signals. The principle utilizes sharp RF permeability changes in a soft magnetic film due to a weak external field. This variation is caused by both magnetization rotation and ferromagnetic resonance. A magnetic readout head which operates on this novel principle has been trial-fabricated. The prototype head was evaluated using sinusoidal signals (0.5 to 10 MHz) which were saturation-recorded on a magnetic tape with a ferrite ring head (head gap 0.3 μm, track width 100 μm). The signal level reproduced at 0.5 MHz by the prototype head was at least 35.7 dB higher than that from a ring head, and for 5-MHz signals the output was from 17.6 to 22.5 dB higher. The carrier-to-noise ratio for a 5 MHz carrier (1 μm wavelength) was from 44 to 47 dB, and was independent of the Ni-Fe film thickness.

articleTitle: High Frequency Magnetic Properties of Co-Based Amorphous Wound Cores Used for Controlling a Switched-Mode Power Supply
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties, and especially the core losses at near-saturation, of Co-Fe-Si-B system amorphous wound cores with various squarenesses are reported. Under ac magnetization at 50 kHz, when control current is zero the core loss increased with the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Lm</inf>, while core losses were lower for samples with higher dc B-H loop squarenesses B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>/B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>. When control current is zero, it is thought that for magnetic amplifier cores, core losses must also be understood, and that a high B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>/B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is useful in lowering core losses at or near core saturation.

articleTitle: Behavior of an Inclinosensor Using Magnetic Fluid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on investigation of the operating mechanism and basic features of a differential output type two-dimensional inclinosensor with a simple configuration based on the combination of a magnetic fluid (MF) and a magnetic core. Optimal MF volume at which output is maximal was found to be 0.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The experiment showed that it is possible to measure a two-dimensional inclined angle from the differential output power with respect to the horizontal angle and the gradient angle.

articleTitle: Magnetization Properties of CoCr Sputtered Films on Polyimide Substrates
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoCr films were formed by sputtering on polyimide substrate at room temperature and at 190°C, and the effects of a substrate bias voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> and a focusing magnetic field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> were investigated. Of films formed at room temperature, the anisotropy field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>, perpendicular anisotropy energy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> and X-ray diffracted intensity were maximum at a substrate bias voltage of -50 V, and the coercivity and Δθ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> were minimum. A small negative bias was found to improve the film c-axis orientation. A Bitter pattern from such a film sample is also shown.

articleTitle: Magnetic Read-out Head Using Induced RF Permeability Variation in Ni-Fe Thin Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A field-sensitive type single pole read-out head was trial-fabricated and its characteristics were studied. Play-back sensitivity in the lower recording frequency region declined as the thickness of the Ni-Fe film decreased, but in the higher recording frequency region the read-out output level was independent of Ni-Fe film thickness maintaining an almost constant level, much higher than conventional heads. The carrier-to-noise ratio is also good. These two results show that this type of head is well suited to highly sensitive magnetic read-out heads for high-density magnetic recording.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Si Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A detailed investigation of the relation between the differences in Fe-Si film structure governing its soft magnetic properties and film magnetic properties is discussed. The absolute values of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> showed extreme variation with different growth conditions. The composition for which H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> was minimal was 7 to 8 wt% Si at 3.5 kV, but at 2.0 kV it was displaced to the high-Si-content side. In-plane anisotropy was independent of film growth conditions, and it was found that the films had strong uniaxial anisotropy of 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> erg/cc. This fact implies that Fe-Si system sputtered film soft magnetic properties are strongly governed by magnetostriction. SEM photomicrograms of film cross sections revealed a columnar structure at 3.5 kV and tapered crystal grains with voids at 2.0 kV. Also, at 3.5 kV the (110) plane was oriented parallel to the film surface, but at 2.0 kV this orientation was disturbed and it was almost random.

articleTitle: Improvement of Lifetimes of Magneto-Optical Disks by Alloying Various Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Various elements were added to TbFe and TbFeCo films and their effects were studied. The addition of Al, Ti, Cr, or Pt was found to inhibit both pinhole growth and corrosion. The addition of Pt not only increased the Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>), but also completely halted the deterioration of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetostriction on External Load by F.E.M.
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Noiseless electrical machinery has been required, but effective countermeasures to noise in electrical machinery have not yet been devised. The main factor causing noise and vibrations in transformers is the magnetostriction, which is very sensitive to stress and heat. This paper deals with analysis of the magnetostriction under an external load using the finite element method (FEM). The magnetostriction induced in a one-dimensional model by stress and magnetic flux densities is analyzed.

articleTitle: Growth-Induced Birefringence of Bi-Substituted Iron Garnet Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Investigations into the relation between the growth-induced birefringence (Δn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup>) and Bi content in Bi garnet films are discussed. BiYMIG (M = Ga, A1) and YIG films were grown by the usual LPE method on {111}GGG substrates. Films with different Bi contents were grown by adjusting the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (= Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) and Rs (= PbO/Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) parameters and the growth temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sub> = 800 to 900°C). The growth- induced birefringence Δn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup> was obtained by analyzing the dependence of TE-TM conversion efficiency on the light propagation distance. In contrast to θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>, Δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sup> does not depend on the amount of Ga or A1 present. The conclusion was that growth-induced birefringence in this system was due to the inhomogeneous distribution of Bi in the dodecahedral sites.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Mn-Sb Multilyered Films with Artificial Superstructure
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multilayered films were prepared by alternating deposition of Mn and Sb in ultra-high vacuum. On deposition, Mn atoms reacted with Sb atoms to form a ferromagnetic compound, MnSb, at the interface. The MnSb layers grow epitaxially on thick Sb layers. By utilizing this epitaxy, ultrathin (less than 10 A) MnSb layers can be sandwiched between thick (50 Å) Sb layers. The resulting superlattice films are ferromagnetic even when each MnSb layer thickness is less than 5 Å.

articleTitle: Amorphous Tb-Fe-Co/Iron Garnet Composite Films On Glass Substrates
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of Bi-substituted iron garnet film and amorphous Tb-Fe-Co film, grown individually and in composite, were investigated. The Kerr rotation of the composite film is explained by the glass and film surface reflection and interference effect in garnet film. In the recorded area, the fine domain structure and the shape were improved in the composite film. The authors conclude that by varying the composition of the garnet film, it is possible to eliminate the reverse-direction domains of the garnet film visible behind the composite film recorded domains and further to improve their shape.

articleTitle: Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy in Ordered Sendust Alloys Single Crystal
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dependence of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> on composition and temperature was studied. A difference of an entire order of magnitude in the maximum K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> value for the slightly different compositions 8.5 wt% Si, 5.0 wt% Al, bal. Fe sample and the 7.5 wt% Si, 6.8 wt% Al, bal. Fe was found, and the difference between their T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K1=0</inf> (temperature at which K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> is zero) was a high 300°C. Other results showed that the effect of thermal processing varies dramatically with only slight change in composition.

articleTitle: Dependence of the Magnetization on the Layer Thickness in Compositionally Modulated Fe/Y Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Compositionally modulated thin films of Fe and Y--which normally form an amorphous alloy--were fabricated to investigate the variation in magnetism with the thickness of each layer. It was found that magnetization disappeared at d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub> ≳2.4 Å, corresponding to a Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub> Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub> composition alloy, agreeing with an Fe-Y amorphous alloy critical composition. When 6 Å ≳ d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub> ≳ 12 Å, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> was almost constant with respect to d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub>. The central region of the Fe layer was composed of pure Fe but had reduced magnetization. This structure is peculiar to compositionally modulated films.

articleTitle: On Detection of Air-Gap Flux and Torque in An Induction Motor Using An Amorphous Ribbon
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors studied the possibility of using the Hall effect in an amorphous ribbon to detect the gap magnetic flux and torque in an induction motor. The ribbon (Hall coefficient R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> = 4.93 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/C) was positioned for maximum sensitivity. Detection characteristics for several methods were compared and detection using the Hall effect was verified to be possible.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Compositionally Modulated RE-po Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fabrication of Nd-Co compositionally modulated thin films with strong magnetization and high anisotropy were studied. Nd thickness was fixed while the Co thickness was varied. It was found that saturation magnetism was the same as that for amorphous films, but K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u⊥</sub> was not the same, samples with high Nd content showing high anisotropy. At room temperature anisotropy of samples with Nd/Co of 1 : 2 is low and the film shows in-plane magnetization, but at 77 K the film is perpendicularly magnetized.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Application of Artificial-Amorphous-Lattice Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Superlattices have been prepared successfully by amorphous materials using dual sputtering system in a wide variety of modulation wavelengths and various combinations. Modulation wavelengths of these films have a significant effect on these structures and the magnetic properties. The thermal stability has been evaluated by measuring the effective interdiffusivity as a function of modulation wavelength and temperature. These amorphous superlattices have been demonstrated to be promising candidates for producing a new class of magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Composition Modulated Amorphous Zr-Fe/Tb-Fe Multilayered Films Prepared by RF Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The changes in structure and saturation magnetization (4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) due to composition modulation period (D), Curie temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>), perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>), and polar Kerr rotation in composition modulated multilayered films with amorphous Zr-Fe films and amorphous Tb-Fe films superimposed were studied. It was found that as D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, the composition modulation period calculated from the first X-ray diffraction peak, gets thinner, 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> increases. This can be explained by the fact that magnetization of Fe within the Zr-Fe film is induced by the Tb-Fe film.

articleTitle: Barkhausen Noise in Yoke Type MR Heads (I)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan

articleTitle: Magneto-optic Transfer Readout Head Using Garnet Film with Periodical Arrangement of Grooves
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magneto-optic transfer readout head with garnet film with grooves formed at appropriate intervals in the surface to suppress displacement of linear domains that causes irregular variation in signal amplitude and noise level was studied. It was found that reducing the spot diameter for use on garnet film with domains of narrow width significantly improved the characteristics.
