This also greatly reduced the instability at readout, and C/N ≃ 50dB was obtained at 5MHz. It was also found that polarized noise is prominent over a wide range.

articleTitle: Study of P-R Segment Using Magnetocardiographic Measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetocardiographic measurement and analysis of P-R segments were studied using a SQUID fluxmeter in a PTB high performance magnetically shielded room. It was found that auricle depolarization and repolarization processes could be clearly distinguished by the difference in polarity on the equivalent magnetic field distribution, and the equivalent potential difference distribution maps. This confirmed that performing analysis of PR segments makes a valuable contribution to research on cardiomagnetism.

articleTitle: Co Ferrite Films by Evaporation Technique in O2 Plasma
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Growth of Co ferrite film by evaporating FeCo alloy in an oxygen plasma was studied. Film grown on glass substrates was polycrystaline with a (100) axis preferential orientation. Film formed on spinel substrate showed epitaxial growth on the (100) axis, and there was a slight difference with the observed bulk diffraction angle. This seems to be due to oxygen deficiency, since compensating for it eliminated the difference. Oxidation of the films formed on the glass substrates due to heat treatment and stress resulted in the films being perpendicularly magnetized as the saturation magnetization increased.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a Perpendicular Magnetic Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Large-scale models of a single pole type perpendicular recording head, as well as actual-size prototype heads, are constructed, and the dependences of the normalized playback output on the main pole length, track width and main pole permeability are compared. The results obtained using the model agree well with the results for the prototype heads. Such models can be useful in studying the characteristics of single pole type heads. It is concluded that a narrower track width is more effective in increasing the playback output than is a higher main pole permeability.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetization of Sputtered CoNx Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of a substrate bias voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> applied during reactive sputtering of CoN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> films, and of the N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> partial pressure fraction r, on the perpendicular magnetization properties of the films were investigated. Appropriate choice of r and V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> enable fabrication of perpendicular magnetization films (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k⊥</sub> > 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>); and the higher the input power and smaller the substrate-target distance, the gentler the changes in film magnetic properties with r and V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Amorphous Metal Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The properties of Fe-Si-B system and Co-Fe-Si-B system wires were studied. B-H loops of the wires varied greatly with applied magnetic field and sample length. At lengths greater than 5 cm peculiarly large Barkhausen effects appeared. It was discovered that driving an ac current through the wires induced a reverse Matteucci effect. The phases reverse with direction in which the wire is twisted, and this seems to be due to the fact that the directions of the domain walls change with the twisting angle which occurs due to the circumference field induced by the current flowing within the wire.

articleTitle: Iron Loss of Supermalloy Film Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The suitability of a supermalloy thin film about 1 μm thick for use in 1 MHz power equipment was studied. The relationship between the hysteresis loss W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> and the maximum flux density B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> for the approximately 1 μm thick films deposited on SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> substrate is approximately W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> ∝ B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.75</sup>. This shows the same tendency as that for the rolled plate, where W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> ∝ B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.6</sup>, but the hysteresis loss value is one order of magnitude greater. In conventional rolled tape, the hysteresis loss is inversely proportional to tape thickness, but in the case of thin films, W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> obstructs any large-scale reduction in the loss.

articleTitle: Sputtered Fe-Si-Al Alloy Film Video Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Read/write characteristics of a prototype narrow-track video head using sputtered Fe-Si-Al alloy thick film were studied. The I/O characteristics showed that recording capability is sufficiently high, and read-out output exceeded that of a ferrite head per unit coil turn and unit track width, demonstrating that both parameters of the prototype head are sufficient for practical applications. It was also found that playback demagnetization loss was less than 1 dB per 100 passes.

articleTitle: Reliability of Magneto-Optical Memory Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: TbFeCo recording layers were deposited onto polycarbonate (PC) and PMMA substrate disks and their characteristics were examined and compared. The more durable PC substrate disks had lower C/N ratios than the PMMA disks. The use of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> protective layers improved the bit-error rate (BER) of the PC substrates from 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> to 7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>, and there was no changes in the C/N ratios even after 1000 h.

articleTitle: Calculation of Hysteresis Loss by Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors propose a set of functions to approximate hysteresis loops in calculations of hysteresis losses by the finite element method, which are modifications of the approximating function of Potter et al, to broaden the range of applicability. The results of actual calculations using this method for the hysteresis loss distribution in a two-legged transformer are indicated.

articleTitle: DyBi Garnet Films with Improved Temperature Dependence of Faraday Rotation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of host rare-earth ions (Dy, Gd, Yb) on Bi-substituted garnet film Faraday rotation coefficient (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>) variation with temperature were investigated in an effort to improve the isolation of such media used in optical isolators. Even when semiconductor laser wavelength fluctuations (1.310 ± 0.0025 μm) due to environmental temperature change were taken into consideration, observations and calculations showed that in the temperature range 0 to 50°C, the theoretical isolation value for Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> can exceed 29 dB. The authors determined that (DyBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> epitaxial film Faraday rotation coefficient (-900 deg/cm, 1.3 μm) has low temperature variation when used as isolator material.

articleTitle: Surface Protective Film for CoNiCr/Cr Sputter Hard Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Surface protective films for hard disk media were studied. Whereas sputtered carbon films are not sufficiently wear-resistant for use with CaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. TiC head sliders, tests using plasma-CVD films prepared in acetylene gas under RF or dc discharge have lubricating properties and sufficient wear resistance, but are so soft that disk surfaces are easily damaged. By combining the two in a double-layer protective film, however, both good wear resistance and low friction when used with the above types of heads are achieved.

articleTitle: Effects of Ar Pressure and Substrate Bias on TbCo Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of Ar pressure on the magnetic characteristics and structure of TbCo sputtered film was studied using bias voltages of 0, -50, and -100 V as parameters. In zero bias films, varying the Ar pressure caused different types of stress (tensile or compressive) as well as structural changes in these films. The Tb atomic density in the films made while alternating the bias voltage between 0 and -100 V was modulated, and these modulated films had perpendicular magnetization characteristics.

articleTitle: Corrosion Resistance of Magneto-Optical Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of adding Ti to TbFe and TbCoFe films with and without protective layers were studied. The addition of Ti improved the corrosion resistance of the films more effectively than an SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> protective layer. 10 percent Ti tripled the corrosion resistance of TbFe films and doubled that of TbCoFe films. Pit formation during aging and immersion in brine was eliminated almost completely by the addition of 5 percent Ti, which also increased the Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) slightly in TbFe and TbCoFe films. 10 percent Ti lowered θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> somewhat while improving the corrosion resistance.

articleTitle: Write Spacing Loss in Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A relatively simple method is introduced to form microspacing between a probe-type head and a Co-Cr/Ni-Fe double-layer medium to investigate the effects of submicron spacing on perpendicular magnetic recording characteristics. It was shown experimentally that, as the spacing becomes large in recording, the reproduced voltage in saturation recording decreases. This phenomenon may be caused by the following: with increasing spacing, the recorded magnetization transition width in the medium is lengthened by decreasing write head field gradient resulting from the disappearance of the main pole-to-medium magnetic interaction.

articleTitle: Structure Dependence of Magnetic Properties for Compositionally Modulated Films Including Rare Earth Metals as a Constituent
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of magnetic properties on the layer structure of compositionally modulated Gd-Fe and Y-Fe films has been studied. It was found that by varying the periodicity of alternating layers, the structure of each layer can be controlled in a continuous way. In Gd-Fe films, samples with a period of less than 20 Å show a perpendicular anisotropy similar to that seen in amorphous film prepared by simultaneous evaporation, while films with each layer thickness 40 Å exhibit a "compensation temperature" due to a ferrimagnetic coupling between Gd and Fe layers. The magnetic behavior of Y-Fe films reflects changes in the structure more clearly than in the case of Gd-Fe system films. There exists a critical thickness for the Fe layer to complete a bcc structure. Below a critical thickness of 20 Å, the Fe layer is amorphous in nature; this, however, only occurs when the Fe layer is sandwiched between Y layers. Finally, recent studies on single crystal rare earth superlattices, including the Gd-Y and Dy-Y systems, are briefly reviewed.

articleTitle: Thick-Film Crystal Growth of Highly Bi-Substituted Garnet for Optical Isolators
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We studied the melt composition to obtain pit-free, highly Bi-substituted (BiLu)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> crystals by the LPE method. It was confirmed that adding B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> to the melt increases the equilibrium segregation coefficient of Bi K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(Bi)</sub>, and we found that a decrease in garnet composition ratio R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> acts to increase the growth rate dependence of the normalized effective segregation coefficient of Bi K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff(Bi)</sub>/ K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(Bi)</sub>. It was also found that crystals with mirror-smooth surfaces could be obtained by adding Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> to the melt. Using a melt with Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/Lu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> ≥ 1, the pits which usually appear in LPE growth of (BiLu)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> were eliminated, and pit-free, highly Bi-substituted (BiLuGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> crystals were obtained. The optical properties of 250 μm thick (BiLuGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> crystals were measured in order to evaluate their applicability to optical isolators for use at 1.3 μm. A sufficient Faraday rotation of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> = -1800 deg/cm and an extinction ratio of -40 dB were obtained.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of Compositionally Modulated Fe/Y Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Structures of compositionally modulated Fe/Y films were studied by thermal analysis. The exothermic peak found in the DSC curve of (Fe 12 Å/Y 12 Å) most probably corresponds to crystallization of an amorphous material. SEM analysis suggested that the composition of crystallized (Fe 12 Å/Y 12 Å) was YFe2. It is concluded that a compositionally modulated (Fe 12 Å/Y 12 Å) is amorphous in structure as well as in magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Effects of Tetrahedrally Coordinated Co2+ in Ferrites
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A large magneto-optical effect near the 0.7 and 1.5 μm wavelengths in ferrites containing tetrahedral Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions was studied on the basis of crystal field theory, and the calculated spectrum described herein was found to essentially reproduce the experimentally observed Faraday rotation curves of the Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ion substituted ferrites. Eigenstates corresponding to the 0.7 and 1.5 μm transitions were determined in the framework of the strong crystal field approximation, using data for the absorption spectra of tetrahedral Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions in the garnets. The strengths of these transitions and the spin-orbit interaction coefficients of the excited states were calculated from the eigenstates. From these parameters, the Faraday rotation spectrum was calculated for the wavelength range from 0.5 to 2.0 μm.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Carrier to Noise Ratio in Perpendicular Magnetic Recording with Narrow Track-Width Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Actual examples are given to show that low head impedance is extremely important in narrow track-width heads for high-density perpendicular magnetic video recording and reproduction, and that it strongly affects the wideband frequency characteristics and the noise level of the head. A main pole excitation probe-type head (MPD), with 7 μm track width, was fabricated to compare the dependence of frequency band and noise characteristics on head impedance. With high sensitivity and low impedance, the MPD head had a very favorable CN ratio of 54.5 dB, suggesting that in the future it will provide significant advantages for widebanddigital recording.

articleTitle: Charged Wall Behavior Observed by Bubble Run-Out Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new potential well measurement method, utilizing bubble run-out phenomena, is discussed, with emphasis on its application in observing charged wall behavior, as well as in measuring the potential well depth itself. The method is applied to bubbles in ion implanted propagation patterns on 1 μm bubble garnet films with different magnetostriction constants. Bubble run-out directions are found to be reflected by the strength of stress relaxation-induced magnetic anisotropies along ion-implantation pattern edges. The charged wall length and its stray field distribution were also estimated using this method. It is concluded that this method is one of the most useful tools available for operation error mode analysis in ion-implanted bubble device development.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Magnetic Recording Media Noise
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A modified version of the Thurlings method, compensated for fluctuations in magnetization direction and magnetic powder filling density, is used as a theoretical formalization of modulation noise in magnetic recording media which is considered to be generated by magnetization direction variation in the transition region. The results of the simulation are compared with actual measurements on thin-film media. Close correspondence was found between calculations and actual measurements of modulation noise in magnetic thin-film media, showing an increase with respect to recording density at a rate of 3 dB/Oct. under saturated recording.

articleTitle: Transient Response in a Converter Controlled by a Magnetic Amplifier
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relationship between the magnetic characteristics of a saturable reactor core and its transient response in converters controlled by magnetic amplifiers is presented. The linear operating region in the converters depends on the permeability μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> in the saturation region of the saturable reactor core. It was found that excellent transient response can be obtained by using a low μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> core.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Loss in Thinned Single Crystals of 3% Si-Fe
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between the inclination angle of the [001] axis ß and hysteresis loss in Si-Fe single crystal sheets was studied. No appreciable increase in the range 0° to 2° was found, but from 2° to 3° rapid increase was observed. This seems to be due to the facts that when ß is in the low angle range below 2°, surface closure domains exist separately and independently, and above 2° the closure domains couple together and form an aggregate structure.

articleTitle: Structures of One-Dimensional Charged Walls
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To improve on the resolution of previous calculations of charged domain wall structures in ion-implanted films, further calculations were performed on the structures of one-dimensional charged walls. Calculations relied on numerical integration of the magnetization equation of motion, for an appropriate initial distribution. The distributions of the angle made by the magnetization with the implantation edge and with the direction normal to the film, as well as the magnetic charge distribution, were determined for different external fields.

articleTitle: Fundamental Characteristics of a New Torque Sensor of Circumferential Excitation Type
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The operating characteristics of a new type of torque sensor are described. The sensor consists of amorphous ribbons endowed with uniaxial anisotropy bonded to the shaft and corresponding pick-up heads. The heads are excited at 50kHz. The output signals from the sensors are processed to produce burst signals from which the torque is obtained. This sensor is easily mounted on a shaft, has a high detection sensitivity and operates under a low exciting current. It can be used to detect the torque at a given angular displacement, or for simultaneous detection of torque and revolution rate.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Proximity Sensor Using a Planar-Type Micro-Magnetic Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Whereas most proximity sensors are sensitive to a single physical quantity, the authors describe a sensor employing a planar micro-magnetic core of thermosensitive amorphous magnetic ribbon which is sensitive to both heat and magnetic fields. Experimental values were in reasonably good agreement with results calculated from the equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: 1.3 μLD Module with Optical Isolator Using YIG Crystals by the Floating Zone Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on fabrication of an LD (laser diode) module with an optical isolator using YIG crystals in which the optical parts are fixed by soldering and YAG laser welding. The LD to single-mode fiber coupling efficiency was less than -4.6 dB, and the isolator insertion loss was 0.1 dB. Output variation in the 0 to 50°C temperature range was as low as 0.4 dB and after heat treatment, coupling loss variation was less than 0.25 dB, a very stable value. This seems to be due to the fact that the optical fiber and the lens were fixed by the metal fixing methods. Laser output noise induced by the reflected laser beam from the far end of the single-mode fiber is reduced by the optical isolator. Using YIG made by the FZ method and fabricating the module using the metal fixing methods realizes high isolation ratio and high reliability.

articleTitle: Properties of SmCo Film for Magnetic Rotary Encoder
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: RF magnetron sputtering was used to prepare SmCo films on drums for use in magnetic rotary encoders and the recording and playback characteristics were investigated. It was found that for a head-medium spacing of 15 μm, recording and playback with an S/N ratio of at least 30 dB was possible at bit lengths as short as 50 μm, corresponding to a maximum resolution of approximately 3150 PPR when adopted in ordinary 50 mm diameter encoders.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties Of Co-Substituted Garnet Films Prepared By Pyrolisis Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Ge was substituted in Co-substituted garnet film with no composition disparity to introduce Ge quadrivalent ions to compensate for the charges of the Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions. Co substitution increases the crystallization temperature while Ge substitution has the reverse effect. Faraday rotation coefficient measurements confirmed the existence of Co divalent ions in tetrahedral sites.

articleTitle: High-Density Information Storage by Means of Magnetic Holography of Amorphous TbFe Thin Films (II)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Previously we reported the possibility of recording information by means of magnetic holography (using amorphous TbFe thin films as a hologram medium) onto a spot of diameter less than 1 mm, reconstructing data using the Faraday effect. However, we had not studied the basic characteristics of information storage in detail, and therefore were not able to make good-quality holograms with good reproducibility. Because reproducibility is the characteristic of greatest importance for recording, we studied the recording margin for information storage by magnetic holography. In addition, we considered the relationship between the power density of the two beams (object beam and reference beam) and the domain pattern (hologram). It was confirmed that the domain pattern is closely related to the beam density, and the recording margin depends on the information pattern. From these results, we were able to create good-quality holograms with satisfactory reproducibility.

articleTitle: Oxidation on Target Surface in RF Sputtering of Iron Targets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To investigate the sudden change in deposition rate and film structure at a critical value of the oxygen gas partial pressure (Po<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) during reactive sputtering of iron targets, the authors formed film at various rf input powers, while measuring the temperature of a thermocouple placed between target and substrate. A hysteresis effect in the temperature with respect to input power was found, which was concluded to correspond to oxidation of the target surface, and corresponding increased emission of secondary electrons. Changes in the hysteresis loop with increasing pressure Po<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> supported this hypothesis.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of YFe, (Gd, Tb)-YFe Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: YFe sputtered films were studied to clarify the behavior of Fe-Fe interactions in an amorphous RE-Fe matrix. The effect of the RE magnetism on the magnetic properties of RE-Fe films was also investigated using (Gd, Tb)-YFe sputtered films. Amorphous YFe films exhibit spin-glass like characteristics, that is, the magnetization does not saturate easily even at low temperatures because of the noncollinear alignment of the Fe moments. The addition of an RE element (Gd, Tb) to YFe film serves to eliminate the spin-glass like nature, and a magnetically ordered state can be observed. The exchange interaction between the RE element and Fe may play an important role in RE-YFe film.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of Perpendicular Magnetic Rocording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Self-consistent vector magnetization distributions were obtained using a magnetization model for single domain ferromagnetic fine particles modified to generate the actual two-dimensional M-H curve of a recording medium. This formed the basis of a computer simulation capable of explaining the magnetization state within the media and the recording/reproducing characteristics relatively well. Comparing the results obtained from the simulation model with actual measurements confirmed that it is effective.

articleTitle: Rolled Texture and Magnetic Properties of Rapidly Quenched Silicon Steel
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The variation of magnetic properties of high-silicon steel with rolling and annealing were studied. It was found that flux density decreased monotonically as the roll reduction rate was increased to the neighborhood of 40 percent, but then rapidly increased as roll reduction was increased beyond this, reaching an almost constant value of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> = 1.68 T, suggesting that when the roll reduction rate is greater than 50 percent, the degree of alignment of the [001] axis to the rolling direction increases.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy in H2+ Implanted (100), (110) Garnet Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantation on magnetic anisotropy in (100) and (110) garnet films were studied by ferromagnetic resonance, and compared with results for helium implantation. The ``hydrogen effect", a large increase in the effective uniaxial anisotropy field with hydrogen implantation in (111) films, was not observed in (100) films. It is concluded that the hydrogen effect brings about an apparent increase in the magnetostriction constants, and particularly in λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub>.

articleTitle: Influence of Sputtering Conditions on Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy in GdTbCo Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of Ar pressure on GdTbCo film characteristics without bias voltage were studied. Sample films demonstrated a large perpendicular anisotropy (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>) which increased with the Tb contraction. In GdCo films, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> became less negative as the Ar pressure increased, but K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> decreased in films containing Tb. Other results indicated that GdTbCo disks will be easy to manufacture.

articleTitle: Physical Considerations on Magnetostatic Energy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The author considers there are ambiguities surrounding usage of the terms ``demagnetizing energy" and ``magnetostatic energy", taking as a concrete example the physics of magnetic bubbles. Here, on considering the bubble region only, a difference in sign arises between the magnetic potential energy (negative) and the demagnetizing energy (positive). Considerations of a cylindrical magnetic body in the saturated state also turn up discrepancy arising from the use of the concept of a demagnetizing field. It is concluded that concepts such as magnetic charge and demagnetizing field may be useful for convenience's sake, but must not be used in interpreting actual physical situations.

articleTitle: DyBi Garnet Films with Improved Temperature Dependence of Faraday Rotation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To improve the temperature dependence of the isolation value of magneto-optical Bi-substituted garnet films for use in optical isolators, the temperature dependence of the Faraday rotation coefficient was measured for (RBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (R = Dy, Gd, Yb) and (GdBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (FeAlGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> films in the 1.3 and 1.5 μm wavelength bands. Among the various compositions of Bi-substituted garnet films examined, the Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> films showed a 2 percent shift in Faraday rotation from that measured at 25°C and an isolation figure of 36 dB in the temperature range from 0 to 50°C. An isolation figure of 29 dB is assured even if the incident light wavelength fluctuates due to the ambient temperature and manufacturing tolerances. These values correspond to those of Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> bulk single crystals. From the viewpoint of material design, the temperature dependence of the Faraday rotation for Bi-substituted garnets is improved by employing a solid solution with a rare-earth garnet which has a positive Faraday rotation and a negative temperature coefficient of Faraday rotation at room temperature.

articleTitle: High Density Perpendicular Magnetic Recording by Ring Head and Vacuum-Deposited Co-Cr Single-Layer Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Investigations using narrow gap ferrite video heads and vacuum-deposited Co-Cr single-layer media are reported. The characteristics of ring head and single-layer film combinations, in particular the perpendicular recording capability, were discussed from the point of view of the di-pulse ratio (DPR) of isolated transitions. It was found that although ring head perpendicular recording capability declines as the gap length is reduced, and the isolated pulse's DPR itself gets smaller, reduction in recording demagnetization due to reduction in gap length actually improved the recording density.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Asymmetrical Waveform in Digital Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Waveform distortion reduces the phase detection margin in digital magnetic recording systems. Experimental and theoretical investigations into the relation between recording characteristics and waveform distortion of a thin-film head and a sputtered γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> disk were performed. Recording current and waveform distortion were measured after the DC-erase, in both directions. It was found that magnetic recording waveform distortion is related to the overwrite characteristics, such that the overwrite value must be maintained at a minimum of 30 dB to keep waveform distortion within 2 ns.

articleTitle: Loss Reduction of a Multi-Input Transformer in a Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Making power supplies more compact by reducing transformer distributed capacitance which will in turn reduce loss is discussed. This is especially important for the multi-input transformers in flyback converters. It was found that the so-called sandwich winding, with a low-voltage winding and a secondary winding inserted between high-voltage windings, is effective for this purpose. Transformer loss can be reduced by about 17 percent by decreasing the distributed capacitance.

articleTitle: Effects of Ion-Implantation in Magnetic Garnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Ion implantation in magnetic garnet films induces anisotropy field change ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>. The primary origin of the ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> is the stress-induced anisotropy, but it has been reported that ion implantation also induces nonmagnetostrictive anisotropy change due to growth-induced anisotropy suppression. Hydrogen ion implantation induces a large ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> due to the chemical effects of the hydrogen in the implanted layer. The ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> in ion-implanted garnet is significantly increased by exposing implanted films to plasma of hydrogen or rare gases. These large anisotropy changes in hydrogen implantation and plasma exposure are attributed to the change in valence state of Fe ions. This reports reviews these recent developments on ion-implanted garnets.

articleTitle: Crystal Orientation and Magnetic Properties in Thin-Gauge Silicon-Iron Sheets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of magnetic properties on sheet thickness of polycrystal thin-gauge silicon-iron sheets was studied under application of tensile stress. It was confirmed that iron loss decreases as crystal orientation improves at low thicknesses. Application of high tensile stress in the thin-gauge range does have an effect in reducing hysteresis loss.

articleTitle: Effect of Plasma Exposure on Magnetic Properties of Ion-implanted Bubble Garnet Film with Suppression of Growth-induced Anisotropy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: When ion-implanted garnet crystal films are exposed to plasma, the change in induced anisotropy field ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> is enhanced. The role of growth-induced anisotropy in this effect was investigated by using annealing at 1000°C to suppress growth-induced anisotropy while studying the effect of Ar plasma exposure on Ne<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-implanted films of bubble garnet. The increase in ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> was concluded to be unrelated to any suppression of growth-induced anisotropy, and is thought to originate in an effective increase in the magnetostriction constants.

articleTitle: Characteristics of the Torque Sensor Usins Plasma-Sprayed Ni Layer--Effect of the Heat Treatment of the Ni Layer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magnetostrictive Ni layer, plasma-sprayed onto a shaft, was used in conjunction with a pair of magnetic heads to measure the torque exerted on the shaft. Whereas the as-sprayed film had a high coercivity, annealing for two hours at from 500 to 1000°C lowered the coercivity, and caused the film to become magnetically more homogeneous. An example of the detection of transient fluctuations in the applied torque is also presented.

articleTitle: Fe/Cu Multilayered Thin Films by RF-Magnetron Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on research into the relationship between structure and magnetic properties of Fe/Cu multilayered films grown by the sputtering method in which the Fe and Cu in the system did not have a tendency to form solid solutions with respect to one another. Auger electron spectroscopy analysis and transmission electron microscopy observation showed that these films were periodic multilayered structures. As the thickness of a single layer decreased, the coercivity decreased, and single-axis anistropy in the plane was observed clearly.

articleTitle: Effects of Crystallization Conditions on Magnetic Properties of Crystallized Nd-Fe-B Ribbons
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of crystallization conditions on the magnetic properties of originally amorphous Nd-Fe-B ribbons were investigated. Amorphous Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf> Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</inf> B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> ribbons were obtained by the single-roller quenching technique; these ribbons, with improved ductility and tensile strength, are magnetically soft in the as-prepared state and can be hardened by crystallization. It was found that crystallization by annealing for a short time at high temperatures is desirable to obtain good hard magnetic properties. X-ray diffraction analyses and SEM observations revealed that flash crystallization results in precipitation of sub-micron Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf> B microcrystals, whose sizes are nearly that of a single-domain particle, and which exhibit extremely high coercive forces. Extended annealing at high temperatures causes growth of crystallites and lowering of the coercive force. Ribbons crystallized under optimum conditions are magnetically isotropic with a B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of 7 kG and a (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 10.2 MGOe when magnetzed by a pulse field of about 30 kOe.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties of Amorphous Rare-Earth Transition-Metal Alloy Films at Low Temperatures
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>) and sublattice magnetization (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sub>) of GdFeCo film were studied. θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> could be increased by adding Co to GdFe film to a concentration of approximately 30 percent. Above that point, θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> began to decrease. θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> was essentially proportional to M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sub> through Co concentrations of 50 percent, but above 30 percent, μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> decreased more rapidly than M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sub>.

articleTitle: Operating Characteristics of Magnetic Frequency Multiplier with Core-Type Zero-Phase-Sequence Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new type of magnetic frequency multiplier is proposed for improved performance. This device has core-type output windings installed collectively by combining the cores into a T. The length of output winding of this type of device can be reduced to about 56 percent of the conventional type. The core advantages of this type of magnetic frequency multiplier are as follows: (1) high efficiency equivalent to a large-scale device can be obtained easily; (2) fluctuations in the output voltage can be reduced. In this paper, operation of a core-type frequency multiplier is analyzed by the harmonic balance method considering the unbalance of the circuit. The mechanism of the two-step jumps which occur in the nonlinear zero-phase-sequence circuit is clarified by results of the analysis.

articleTitle: Preparation of Iron Films by Dual Ion Beam Sputtering and Their Soft Magnetic Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The causes of differences in 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> values for iron thin films grown under the same conditions were studied. It was found that H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> reaches a minimum and 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> reaches a maximum when the radiation ion acceleration voltage is in the range 140 to 150 V. But the differences in values of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> seem to be due to impurities like carbon. The presence of wide peaks (thought to be Fe (b.c.c) (200) plane) in the x-ray diffraction diagrams for samples with comparatively high 4μM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> values suggests that the long-distance ordering improvement shown in the x-ray diffraction diagrams relates to the increase in 4μM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> values.

articleTitle: Wide Band Recording Characteristics of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The read after write characteristics of wideband signals for realtime digital video recording and high-speed transmission in perpendicular magnetic recording were compared at different relative velocities. Almost the same normalized output was obtained at relative velocity V = 5.2 m/s and at V = 20.4 m/s, but it was slightly lower at V = 15.6 m/s, going down to the short wavelength range, which seemed to be due to head friction causing slightly bad contact at V = 15.6 m/s resulting in increased space loss. It was found that the wideband C/N variation trends with respect to the relative speeds differ according to the recording wavelength.

articleTitle: Dynamics of Stripe Domain Walls in Bubble Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Computer simulations of the dynamic behavior of domain walls in bubble films, for use in the development of the different functions of Bloch line memories, are commonly based on the domain wall model developed by Slonczewski. To investigate the degree of reliability of this wall model, we compared numerical results of the dynamics of an infinitely long, straight stripe domain with stripe translation measurements, where drive pulses of the order of 2 to 10 Oe and 50 to 200 nsec were applied, and the total displacement of the stripe, including overshoot, was measured. Numerical and experimental results for the total displacement agree well for drive fields below the experimentally determined breakdown field. The values obtained for the breakdown field also agree well in most cases; however, the discrepancy increases with increasing film thickness and drive field strength. Another discrepancy is the numerical result of a strong dependence of the stripe velocity on the drive field after breakdown in the case of thicker films, which was not observed in experiments. Both discrepancies are thought to result from implicit limitations of the wall model.

articleTitle: Simulation of Spacing Between Magnetic Head and Medium on Video Floppy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Unusually wide spacing between two-track magnetic heads of various shapes and a video floppy disk media for still images was simulated to determine how it can be reduced by altering the form of the head to provide the stable, small spacing required in magnetic recording. The system of simultaneous equations, consisting of the lubrication equation for head and medium and the medium deformation and motion equations, was solved using the finite element method. It was found that having a groove more than 2 μm deep and more than 5 μm wide in the sliding surface is effective in reducing the spacing.

articleTitle: High Frequency Transistor Inverter with CT
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The commutation mechanism of high-frequency transistor inverters with a current transformer was studied. The current transformer eliminated the need for dead time in the commutation time, as in the usual procedure. It was also found that storage time can be reduced by connecting an external base resistance and that the storage time can be used for effective switching. However there is a trade off here with such parameters as the oscillation conditions and fall time.

articleTitle: Effect of Selective Tilt for GGG (111) Substrate Surface on the Magnetic Domain in Bubble Garnet LPE Layers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: GGG (111) substrate surfaces are selectively tilted in an attempt to locally stabilize stripe domains. This method utilizes the magnetization easy axis inclination away from [111] in the tilted section. When an in-plane magnetic field (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) is applied to the substrate surfaces in a direction traversing the tilted section, a magnetic field is simultaneously produced in the magnetization easy axis direction of the tilted section. When an external bias magnetic field (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>) is applied in the [111] direction, the effective magnetic field parallel to the magnetization in the tilted section can be modulated by H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>. The results of our experiments demonstrate that this method can be used to simultaneously stabilize both the stripe domains of the tilted sections and the bubbles of the untilted regions at given H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>.

articleTitle: Photoinduced Effect on Surface Modes in H2+-Implanted YIG Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A previous report described the decrease of the surface spin wave resonance field, ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>, with light irradiation of ion-implanted YIG at 77 K. Here the authors describe ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> relaxation as the irradiation is turned on and off, as well as the effect of annealing on ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> for films covered with a sputtered SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer. The time to saturation of ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> with light stimulation was much longer for annealed samples. Changes in ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> normally accompanying annealing (250°C) were found to be almost absent in films covered with an SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer.

articleTitle: Domain and Domain Wall Structures of Layered Magnetic Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The domain and domain wall structures of double-layered Co-Nb-Ti magnetic films, with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films of varying thicknesses interposed between the magnetic layers were studied. It was found that domain and domain wall structures changed as the thickness of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film increased, which can be explained by the change in magnetic coupling between the upper and lower magnetic layers. The coupling between the magnetic layers varied largely within the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thickness range much less than the wall thickness, which differs from the reported results for Permalloy films.

articleTitle: Development of An Amorphous Torque Sensor for Induction Motors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A torque sensor employing amorphous ribbons (FeCoSiB) bonded to the rotor shaft for use in induction motors, is described. Magnetic field annealing is used to induce an anisotropy in the ribbons which were relatively Co-rich composition. By using more than one sensor head, the influence of magnetic fields generated by the motor can be suppressed. Output averaging yielded good linearity, high accuracy (±0.07 kg-m) and satisfactory sensitivity (22.4 mV/kg-m).

articleTitle: Physical Considerations on Magnetic Circuit with an Air-Gap
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The changes in magnetic flux density distribution which occur when air gaps from 1 to 30 mm long are opened in an I-shape magnetic body were measured. The magnetic flux density distribution was found to be shifted relative to the distribution at an isolated end of the body, due to the magnetic interaction between the bodies across the gap. By taking this interaction into account, it is possible to determine the change in flux density due to the gap.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies for Film Structure of TbCo Magnetooptical Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors discuss how the interference layer thicknesses affect the figure of merit (R × θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) of quadrilayer TbCo magneto-optic disks. Disk samples consisted of an Al reflecting layer, a frist Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> interference layer (O.L.), a TbCo recording layer and a second Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> interference layer (U.L.), all of which were sputtered onto transparent substrate. Varying the U.L. thickness had little effect on the reflectance R or Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>, but both changed significantly in response to changes in the O.L. thickness. This result could be attributed to phase differences generated within the O.L. layer.

articleTitle: Heavy Rare-Earth, Co-Substituted Amorphous TbFe Films for Magneto-Optical Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dynamic characteristics such as carrier-to-noise ratio (CNR) of single-layer TbDyFeCo films were studied along with films in which the rare-earth elements Ho and Er were substituted for Dy. The θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> values of TbDyFeCo films were sufficiently large for high rate read/write applications. The Ϙ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> and the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> values of the TbHoFeCo and TbErFeCo films fell within the range of conventional usage.

articleTitle: Plastic Flow and Field Induced Anisotropy in Co-Base Amorphous Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Plastic flow has been investigated in Co-base amorphous alloys with additive elements, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">71</inf> Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf> M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, by creep measurements employing a constant-heating-rate method near the glass transition temperature. The activation energy in the creep process was found to be proportional to the atomic volume of the additive elements, which were determined from the Goldschmidt radius. The observed activation energy varied from 1.92 eV to 2.53 eV, for Co (1.25 Å) and Nb (1.47 Å), respectively. The field-induced anisotropy energy K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> has been measured for the same alloy system. It was found that K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> decreased with increasing atomic volume of non-magnetic additive elements. At nearly the same atomic volumes of additive elements, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> seemed to depend on the strength of the magnetic interaction. From these results, the degree of rearrangement of atoms and the magnetic interaction between magnetic atoms play dominant roles in determining the field-induced magnetic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Kerr and Hall Effects in GdEuCo Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Kerr rotation angle and Hall effect in GdEuCo sputtered films are discussed. The results indicate that the absolute values of the saturation Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup>) varied somewhat at the center and ends of the substrate samples, but these values were maximum around 2 percent Eu. θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup> decreased uniformly above 2 percent Eu. The Hall voltage at saturation magnetization (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup>) reaches a minimum at around 3 percent Eu and then increases, exceeding the value found at 0 percent Eu and exhibits a movement opposite to the Kerr effect. Adding Eu causes either a uniform decrease in Co, or an increase in RE, but there is no such uniform increase or decrease in V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup>.

articleTitle: Relation between Signal Quality and Groove Shape in Magneto-Optical Disk(2)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Calculations and experimental results are described which clarify the relation between signal quality (C/N) and groove shape of magnetic recording media. Calculation indicated a tendency for the C/N ratio to be favorable the wider and shallower the groove, and the experiment results supported this conclusion well. At a groove depth of 15nm there was no appreciable difference in C/N over the disk with no groove, but at a depth of 59nm, C/N was 2 to 4dB smaller. On a disk with a 0.8μm wide, 15nm deep groove, at a recording frequency of 0.24MHz, C/N was 61.3dB, and at 1MHz it was 58.7dB, providing extremely good signals.

articleTitle: Corrosion Resistance Dependence on Ta and Zr Densities in Co-Ta and Co-Zr Alloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Corrosion characteristics of CoZr and CoTa, related to Zr and Ta composition densities, were studied. Corrosion characteristics were analyzed by measuring electrical resistance increase (ΔR/R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>) under 80°C and 85%RH atmosphere. It was confirmed that corrosion rates depended on Zr and Ta densities. Corroded layer thickness X was expressed by the equation X = ßlog(t + 1). It was found these films have excellent corrosion resistance.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction of Amorphous GdFeco Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetostriction in a GdFeCo thin film, produced by replacing a part of the Fe in the GdFe film with Co was measured to determine its contribution to the perpendicular anisotropy of amorphous films. Comparison with previously reported results showed that adding rare earth metals and metaloid elements to FeCo polycrystal to make it amorphous exerts a powerful influence on λs.

articleTitle: SEM Analysis and Temperature Dependence of Faraday Rotation in Bi-Substituted Magnetic Garnets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: SEM analysis was used to investigate the crystal defects affecting the magneto-optical figure of merit and the reverse insertion loss of these single crystals, and the temperature variation of the Faraday rotation coefficient was also measured. The defect analyses showed that Bi itself is more prevalent among the defects than Bi-substituted garnet single crystal composition, and Fe and Gd are low. This seems to be due to the fact that the composition of the solvent used during crystal growth is not uniform. The Faraday rotation coefficient θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> at a wavelength of 0.78 μm in the temperature range from room temperature to 100°C was found to be approximately -0.15%/°C.

articleTitle: Characteristics of DC-AC Interconnection System Using an Orthogonal-Core and an SIT Inverter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The power characteristics of a dc-ac interconnection system using an orthogonal core and a static induction transistor (SIT) inverter were studied. It was found that the power supplied to the ac line can be controlled from zero to its maximum value, by varying the phase angle in the range 90° to 130°, and that the efficiency of the SIT square wave inverter reaches values in the range 90 percent to 97 percent.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of CoTaZr Amorphous Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of the sputtering conditions on the magnetic properties of CoTaZr amorphous films are studied. Varying the input power from 100 to 700 W can vary the Co concentration by as much as 8 at%, or approximately 5 kG when converted to B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>. Varying the bias voltage or argon gas pressure can have similar effects. The permeability of multilayered samples was still inferior to that of single-layer samples, a phenomenon that the authors intend to investigate further.

articleTitle: Recent Research on Bloch Line Memory
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Chip organization of Bloch line memory having major-line minor-loop scheme is presented on the basis of preliminary experiments and computer simulation. The bubble propagation major-line is composed of two level zigzag conductors. Minor-loops are stripe domain walls surrounding completely grooved regions. Practical methods for Bloch line writing and sensing are also presented including stripe domain stretching and initiation.

articleTitle: Bi-Substituted Y-Eu Magnetic Bubble Films with Orthorhombic Anisotropy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The ratio of Y to Eu (= R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>), and the supercooling and film growth temperatures were varied during LPE growth of (YBiEu)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(FeGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> films on the (110) face of NdGG substrate, and the resulting changes in the film orthorhombic anisotropy, the damping constant α, quality factors Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and the wall mobility μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sub> were measured. Under optimized growth conditions, orthorhombic anisotropic film was obtained with Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> = 2.2, Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 1.9, and μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sub> = 16.5 m/s-Oe for 0.9 μm diameter bubbles.

articleTitle: Swap Gate of the Dual Conductor Current Access Device
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Swap gates were designed for dual conductor current access bubble devices, and their performance investigated using an enlarged model and by computer simulations. The enlarged model experiments were used to measure magnetic field distributions; simulations employed parameters for typical (YBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(GaFe)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> bubble films. Driving relies on a sequence of currents, with swap gates operated by changing this sequence. The swap gate pattern was gradually improved through repeated testing, and for a driving current density of 1.5 mA/μm a satisfactory maximum bias margin of 12.3 percent was achieved for operation in all modes.

articleTitle: Torque Sensors for Induction Motors Using Amorphous Microcore Field Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors describe the use of amorphous core sensors as a means of achieving precision vector control in induction motors. This type of sensor detects a magnetic field proportional to the secondary current I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flowing in the rotor end rings to determine the current I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and electric torque. Eight sensor cores are placed around the rotor, reducing the effect of mechanical vibrations. Good output linearity was obtained, and the feasibility of constructing a precision vector control system with a torque feedback loop was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Widening of the Dynamic Range of the Amorphous Torque Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors describe attempts to extend the dynamic range of a torque sensor employing amorphous ribbons, to enable it to measure large momentary torques. The sensitivity and linearity of the sensor varied over a wide range depending on K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>, the anisotropy induced by shear stress in the ribbons. Ribbons were bonded to the shaft transmitting the torque to be measured in various ways. It was found that good linearity could be achieved through choice of an appropriate K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>, enabling extension of the measurable range to large torques.

articleTitle: Bias Voltage Dependence of the Magneto-Optical Effects of Rare Earth-Iron Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It was found that GdTbFe films produced with a bias voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>) of -40 V had a very large Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>). For V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> = -60 V, θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> became extremely small and increased smoothly for V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> ≥ -70 V. The reflectivity (R) reached a maximum at -30 V and decreased beyond that point. This V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> dependence was much stronger in TbFeCo films than GdTbFe films. R spectra indicated that the electron structure of GdTbFe films was unaffected by V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>. In GdTbCo films, the columnar structure became finer as V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> increased. It was concluded that changes in R result from changes in the ratios of high-density and low-density sections of the columnar structure.

articleTitle: Amorphous Tb-Fe Magnetic Thin Films Prepared by Flash Evaporation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Variation in the magnetization curve of amorphous Tb-Fe films prepared by the flash evaporation method while the substrate temperature is varied was studied to clarify the mechanism responsible for perpendicular anisotropy and high coercivity. It was found that a film prepared at a 473 K substrate temperature was a typical perpendicular magnetization film, but in a film prepared at a 77 K substrate temperature, the coercivity and remanence of the hysteresis loop measured in the in-plane direction were both high, suggesting that anisotropy occurs in the in-plane direction.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of R-Ni (R = Gd,Tb,Dy,Ho) Evaporated Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Crystallographic, electrical, and magnetic properties of R-Ni (R = Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho) films were studied. The variation of the electrical resistance with temperature in the R-Ni films was extremely small, indicating that these films do not have the normal crystal structure. This was confirmed by x-ray diffraction patterns which showed that these films were is actually amorphous.

articleTitle: Thick Film Crystal Growth of the Highly Bi-Substituted Garnet for Optical Isolator
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The molar ratio of (Lu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/Lu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> + Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> parameter of the LPE melt for (BiLuGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> growth were varied to determine the region of pit-free thick film growth. The borderline between the presence and absence of pits is in the neighborhood of Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/Lu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> = 1 in the melt. The magneto-optical properties of the 250 μm thick film were studied. 2408°/cm of the Faraday rotation (λ = 1.153 μm) and 37.4 dB of extinction ratio were obtained. This result confirms that it is suitable for compact isolators.

articleTitle: Analysis of Residual Magnetization and Consideration on Demagnetizing Condition of Mild Steel
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The residual magnetic flux distribution in mild steel subjected to magnetization and demagnetization by electromagnets was analyzed from the hysteresis loops, determined using the finite-element method, to find the optimum demagnetizing conditions. It was found that as demagnetizing time increases the demagnetizing effect improves and that when the mild steel was demagnetized under an attenuating alternating field, it was found that the demagnetizing effect optimal frequency is in the neighborhood of 20 Hz.

articleTitle: Characteristics of an Improved Parametric Linear Motor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An improved element was experimentally produced for a parametric linear motor with the magnetic poles positioned on a straight line to overcome the situation in which the shifting magnetic field flux distribution is not homogeneous and good results were obtained.
