It was found that the flux distribution in the improved element was smoother than in the conventional element for a parametric linear motor, and that the flux was more effectively used in the improved element.

articleTitle: Induced Magnetic Anisotropy of CoTi and CoZr Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relaxation process of induced magnetic anisotropy of CoTi and CoZr films is discussed and their permeability compared with that suggested by the single domain theory. The anisotropy energy of the samples was evaluated using the hard and easy axes magnetization curves, and the permeability was measured at 1.4 MHz with the Q meter method. The activation energy of the anisotropy relaxation process in these films was higher than that in CoFeB films, indicating greater thermal stability. The experimental value of the permeability of CoTi films substantially agreed with the predicted values of the single domain theory. A similar results was obtained in CoZr films.

articleTitle: Alumite Disk Using Anodic Oxidation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors describe a process for fabrication of magnetic recording media through formation of an alumite layer by anodic oxidation, and electrodeposition of iron in pores of the cells in the alumite. By varying the voltage and duration of the anodic oxidation, the cell diameter and porosity of the alumite layer can be regulated. Hard disk media were fabricated by this process, which can be applied to flexible disk production also.

articleTitle: Magnetic Characteristics of Fine Permalloy Patterns
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization behavior of patterned Permalloy film used in bubble memory elements is described. A total of 4.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> pattern elements were formed in Permalloy film evaporated onto a GGG substrate, spaced at a period of 4.5 μm. In-plane magnetization curves showed almost no change when a bias field was applied normal to the film, and patterning resulted in a strong shape effect. The in-plane magnetization curves had bends which were attributed to different magnetization characteristics prevailing in different portions of each pattern.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy of Ion-Implanted (100), (110) Garnet Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Anisotropy changes caused by He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantations in (100), (110), and (111) magnetic garnet films have been studied. In (100) films, in striking contrast to (111) films, uniaxial anisotropy field changes were almost the same for He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantations. In (110) films, the orthorhombic anisotropy parameter B changed greatly with H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantations, consistent with anisotropy changes in (111) films. The change in parameter A for He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-implanted (110) films was of the same order as for H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantations. Magnetocrystalline anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implanted films was determined from the angular dependence of (100) in-plane resonance fields. The sign of K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> changed to positive with H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantation. It was found that H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantations have a great effect on λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub> and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, but have little influence on λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</sub>.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Structure for Compositionally Modulated Co-CoOx Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To clarify the influence of CoO spins on the magnetic properties of Co-CoO reactive-sputtered films, Co-CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> compositionally modulated (CM) films were investigated. These Co-CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> CM films were prepared by modulating the oxygen partial pressure (Po<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) in the vacuum chamber. These films have Co-CoO interfaces parallel to the film plane. The coercivity (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) and in-plane anisotropy (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub>) of CM films with short modulation periods increased remarkably below the Néel temperature of CoO (= 292 K). These increases in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> at low temperatures are thought to originate in a magnetic interaction between the Co spins and CoO spins.

articleTitle: Multilayered Garnet Films for High Density Magneto-Optic Memory
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fabrication of multilayered garnet films for magneto-optical recording by the pyrolysis method was investigated. It was found that stress due to differences in thermal expansion coefficients of the bottom layer and substrate reduce the perpendicular anisotropy of the magnetic layer. It was concluded that each layer should be individually crystallized to reduce the influence of dispersion between the layers. This also makes it possible to grow each layer exactly according to design.

articleTitle: Measurement of Magnetic Anisotropy Distribution of a Magneto-Optical Disk by the Hall Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Hall loops of nine square film samples (each size 7 × 7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) cut out along the radius of a magneto-optical disk, were measured under an obliquely-applied magnetic field (H). These measurements indicated that the film magnetization was not completely perpendicular to the film plane, and that the tilt angle of magnetization increased toward the outer edge of the disk.

articleTitle: Bi-substituted DyIG Thin Films Prepared by Chemical Deposition for Magneto-optic Recording Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fabrication of Bi-multisubstituted garnet film on low-cost glass substrates was studied. X-ray diffraction showed that the film was a single-phase polycrystal garnet with no preferred direction. Crystallization temperature decreased as Bi content increases. When Bi was approximately 2mole/f.u., growth was possible at a temperature of around 100°C below that for film growth with no Bi substituted. Calculated values for the stress induced anisotropy caused by the different thermal expansion coefficients of the film and substrate indicated that the perpendicular anisotropy is caused by this stress.

articleTitle: Preparation of Fine Crystalline MnBi Films by Multilayer Structure and their Write-In Characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In this study, the authors attempted to reduce the size of the crystallites of MnBi films through a multilayering process. Three different Bi : Mn ratios and two annealing processes were used. Some of the film samples had M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> values equivalent to single layer films, albeit higher H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. Curie point writing was performed with an external magnetic field of zero and a 25 mW HeNe laser. The pulse widths ranged from 1 μs to 10 μs, and the laser spot was approximately 2 μm in diameter. The size of reversed domains was almost the same as that of the laser spot for pulse widths of 5 to 50 μs.

articleTitle: Structures and Material Characteristics of Magneto-Optical Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of different methods of applying SiO protective layers to magneto-optical disks are discussed. These layers were applied using resistance heating (RH) evaporation, electron beam (EB) evaporation and sputtering. Compositional disparity was observed between the applied films and their sources for each of the different application methods. This disparity was largest with sputtering and smallest with RH evaporation. The aging of the Kerr rotation angle of magneto-optical disks with SiO protective layers also showed a similar correspondence. The continuous production of films with SiO protective layers in a vacuum lowered deterioration levels and inhibited pitting corrosion.

articleTitle: Application of Stochastic FEM in the Analysis of Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The stochastic finite element method designed to deal with indeterminate elements in actual magnetic materials was studied. Permeability is considered as a variable in a homogeneous two-dimensional spatial stochastic process, and the analysis results are compared with those of the usual determinate finite-element method. Both methods produced identical results over a wide range. But the advantage of the probabilistic approach is that the variance can be evaluated directly without performing recursion.

articleTitle: Considerations on the Optimum Design of Small-Sized Parametric Induction Motors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Optimization of the magnetic properties of small output parametric motor materials was studied. Six motors with various combinations of permalloy, ferrites, and silicon steel of the same physical dimensions were fabricated. The authors conclude that isotropic materials, such as ferrite, which easily reaches magnetic saturation, are favorable for the common magnetic circuits, while materials with high saturated flux density, such as silicon steel plate, are appropriate for the excitation magnetic circuits.

articleTitle: Anisotropy Dispersion of Amorphous Co-Metal Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of heat treatment on the anisotropy dispersion of CoZr films was studied. To induce anisotropy, film samples were annealed using a rotating field (RFA) and a direct field (DFA). The sum of the anisotropy field and the demagnetizing field of the DFA film (11.5 Oe) corresponded well with the value of the magnetic field of the distribution peak. The DFA ΔQ half value of less than ±10° indicates a well aligned anisotropy, but the anisotropy of RFA films was dispersed in all directions. The initial anisotropy of these RFA films did not sufficiently relax under the annealing conditions, but prolonging RFA increases the peak width and dispersion and may decrease the macroanisotropy. The anisotropy dispersion of CoFeB and CoTi films is about the same.

articleTitle: Iron Oxygen Based Perpendicular Anistropy Thin Films (Part 2)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Herein are discussed the results obtained in Part 1. The ferromagnetism of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x-y</inf> (M: Si,Co) film samples is attributed to amorphous Fe and Fe-Co phases between column-like oxide structures; these ferromagnetic phases are believed to exist as thin strips directed perpendicular to the film surface, giving rise to an internal shape effect which contributes to the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. Calculations of magnetic moments and of the magnetic anisotropy energy due to the shape effect confirmed this hypothesis.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Amorphous (Fe, Co, Mn)-Y Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic moment m, Curie temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, density ρ, and Young's modulus E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of amorphous Mn-Y, Fe-Y Co-Y, (Fe-Mn)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>, and (Fe-Co)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> alloys fabricated by rapid quenching have been measured to make clear microstructures of amorphous alloys. Detailed comparison of m, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, ρ, and E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> between amorphous alloys and corresponding crystalline compounds, and an X-ray structural analysis reveals a close correlation of an atomic short range order of both states, which is especially found in alloys with Y content less than 30 at%. A structural variation between 30 and 40 at%Y in the Fe-Y amorphous alloys is also indicated by the composition dependence of m, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, ρ, E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and by X-ray structure analysis.

articleTitle: Stability of Ba-Ferrite Magnetic Recording Media.
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Stress and temperature stabilities of Ba-ferrite perpendicular magnetic recording media have been investigated. The stress-induced rate of decrease of remanent magnetization in the media was found to be as small (1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> per kg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) as the values for metal and Co-γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> media. The remanent magnetization in the perpendicular direction remains almost constant in the temperature range from -10 to 80°C. When signals are reproduced with an 8-mm VCR in the still-frame mode, the output decreases after 120 min, and the drop in output after 10 million passes with a 3.5-in floppy disk drive was less than 1 dB. These results confirm the excellent stability of Ba-ferrite recording media.

articleTitle: Numerical Analyses of Recording Charcteristics in Single Pole Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A computer program, developed by the authors for use in numerical analysis of the recording characteristics of single pole heads, was employed to study the effects of the pole material squareness ratio S, a tapered pole shape and a second pole layer, on the reproduced voltage. Results for the dependence on the squareness, which corresponds approximately to the domain inclination angle, agreed with previous experimental results. It was found that both a tapered pole shape and a second layer of thickness at least 3 μm have the effect of raising the reproduced voltage.

articleTitle: Hall Characteristics of RE-TM Amorphous Films with Biaxial Oblique Magnetic Anisotropy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A model of biaxial oblique magnetic anisotropy is presented to explain the irregular ellipse formed by the Hall loop coercive force (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>') versus γ curve in polar coordinates when an oblique magnetic field is applied to high bias sputtered films. It was assumed that the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>' versus γcharacteristics (E) could be demonstrated by averaging the ellipses (E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) generated by the two easy axes (e.a.l and e.a.2). Good correspondence was observed between the measured and calculated values.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties and Stability of TbCo Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of TbCo film samples left in the open air were examined. The bias voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>) of these samples ranged from 0 to -200 V and as the bias voltage became higher, the film structure became more coarse, allowing oxygen to penetrate it and oxidize the Tb atoms. Saturation magnetization of these films occured with time in the vicinity of 550 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It is thought that interface reaction and the diffusion reactions both contribute to this oxidation process. The Faraday rotation angle, nearly constant with time, is thought to be due to the unchanging concentration of the transition metal Co. Changes in the optical constant due to oxidation are thought to cause the increase in θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> of films made at V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> = -150 V.

articleTitle: Brain Magnetic Field Measurement and Model Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: External measurement of magnetic fields generated in the human brain to develop a noncontact and noninvasive observation system of the electrical phenomena occurring within the brain is described. The visual response evoked by a flashed light when it hits the subject's eye is measured by the SQUID fluxmeter at the back of the subject's head. Two current dipole models, one a numerical analysis model used on a computer, and the other a basic experimental model designed to confirm the results of the numerical model, were developed representing the pattern of the brain magnetic field.

articleTitle: Write-Read Characteristics of Magneto-Optical Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In this report, the authors discuss the relationship between peak shift and bit length as they search for ways to lower the bit error rate of magneto-optical disks used in writable/erasable optical memories. The bit error rate of both width recording and edge recording were compared, and it was found that in response to fluctuations in the recording power, edge-recorded information did not change, but width recording fluctuated greatly (approximately 10 percent in response to ±10 percent power fluctuations). Although width recording proved to be better for the same recording capacity, peak shift could be kept down to 1/3 with the edge recording method.

articleTitle: HGMS Filter Performance for Recovery of Magnetic Flocs
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic seed method was used in this study to evaluate the performance of a high-gradient magnetic (HGMS) filter and to investigate the effects of coagulant and pH on the accumulation of magnetic flocs in the filter. It was found that as the concentration of coagulant increased, the initial recovery increased. At a pH of 5.0, the magnetite and silicon dioxide were sufficiently combined that the initial recovery was 100 percent.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of Evaporated Fe-(Pr, Nd) Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic properties and Ker rotation of Fe-light rare earth amorphous film were investigated in order to make clear the factors to determine their magneto-optical effect. Torque measurements on the films were used to determine their temperature and composition dependence of uniaxial anisotropy. It was found that their direction of easy magnetization was perpendicular to the film plane at low temperatures and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> decreased with increasing temperature, changing sign around 200 to 300 K. Finally, it became 0 around 400 K.

articleTitle: High Frequency Permeability of CoNbZr Thin Films Prepared by Tetrode Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new strip-line method for measuring the permeability of CoNbZr thin films at high frequencies (1 ~ 400 MHz) is discussed. Low-frequency measurements (less than 1 MHz) are possible using a coil, but this is impossible at higher frequencies because of the resonance between the coil windings. The strip-line method employs a section of the film sample (in this case 13 mm × 55 mm × 1 μm), a glass epoxy spacer, a glass substrate and a 4191A measuring instrument. Smaller samples (13 × 13 mm) were also tested, but greater film volumes provided better accuracy.

articleTitle: Partially Oxidized Fe-Co Medium with Perpendicular Anisotropy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Partially oxidized FeCo films were prepared by reactive rf magnetron sputtering, and their magnetic properties investigated. Changes in magnetic properties with different O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pressures during sputtering and with Co content are described. The perpendicular magnetic anisotropy exhibited by films was postulated to originate in the shape anisotropy effect due to segregation of paramagnetic oxide material between FeCo grains, and magnetization is believed to occur by rotation. Such films are regarded as promising candidates for use in perpendicular magnetic recording media.

articleTitle: Effects of Ar-ion Implantation Into Ni Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of implanting Ar<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions into Ni films (as opposed to Fe films) on magnetic moment is discussed. The magnetic moment decreased gradually at doses of 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> ions/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> or less and decreased suddenly beyond 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> ions/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. These doses eventually reduce surface tension. Higher doses convert this internal stress back into surface tension. These results support the model that the formation of Ar bubbles generates new Ni interfaces and that this formation of interfaces decreases the Ni magnetic moment.

articleTitle: Effects of Substrate Degassing on Magnetic Properties of CoCr Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of degassing PET, PEN and PI substrates at different temperatures prior to sputter deposition of CoCr films on the film properties, and changes with degassing in the dependence of film properties on the Ar gas pressure during sputtering, were investigated. The effect of the Ar gas pressure on films varies depending on the amount of impurity gases remaining in the substrate, and degassing had a greater effect for PI substrate, which held more impurity gases, than for PET and PEN, in which fewer impurities were present.

articleTitle: Horizontal Incidence Observation of Magnetic Field by Scanning Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for observing magnetic fields is proposed, in which a primary electron beam is directed parallel to the specimen surface. The leakage magnetic field due to recorded magnetization patterns is observed as a secondary electron image using a scanning electron microscope. The secondary electron image consists of different quantities of secondary electrons, depending on whether the primary electron beam is deflected to impinge on the specimen or not as a result of the horizontal component of the leakage magnetic field. Secondary electron images obtained for perpendicular recording and for longitudinal recording are presented. Recording lengths as short as two microns can be resolved by this method.

articleTitle: CMC for Amorphous Magnetic Cores in a 100 kHz-1 MHz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The CMC (control magnetization curves) of amorphous cores, in both toroidal and ring shapes, were measured at frequencies up to 1 MHz. The high-frequency measurements were facilitated by use of a FET dc chopper. The characteristics at 1 MHz, compared with those at lower frequencies, are characterized by a smaller maximum flux density, probably due to core heating, and a narrower region of proportionality. For all samples, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> was found to obey H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> ∝ f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</sup>~f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.1</sup>, where f is the magnetizing frequency.

articleTitle: Relationship Between Magnetization of a Recording Medium and Developing Magnetic Field in Magnetography
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: During development of images in magnetography, the developing magnetic field interacts with the field formed by the latent magnetic image, affecting the resulting image resolution. When the developing field is oriented in the same direction as the image field, the tendency for adhering toner to ``bridge'' the interval between neighboring magnetization transitions is strengthened, and vice-versa if the two fields are aligned in opposite directions. Hence if the developing field direction is not chosen appropriately, white areas in black-white images may be hard to distinguish, lowering the overall resolution.

articleTitle: Composite Type Magnetoresistive Sensor Composed of Ni-Co And Permalloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of reduction in demagnetization field on stripe width, the stability of domain structure, and the magnetoresistive effect in the elements with Ni-Co films and Permalloy films of varying stripe widths were studied. We also investigated the read characteristics of each of the elements. Replacing the conventional structure with a composite structure reduced the demagnetizing field by half, and reduced hysteresis. Since the domain structure approached that of a single domain, it was clear that mutual magnetic effects occurred between the Permalloy film and the Ni-Co film.

articleTitle: Role of Cr3+ on Perpenedicular Magnetic Anisotropy in CoCr Ferrite Thin Films for Magneto-Optic Memory
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The contribution of Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> substitution to perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in CoCr ferrite film fabricated by varying the Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> substitution amount was studied. As the Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> content increased in the CoCr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (x = 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25) films, saturation magnetic field decreased and the squareness ratio increased, showing the increase of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. Films with x greater than 1 had magnetic easy axis perpendicular to the film plane. This result is related to the fact that as Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> substitution amount increased, saturation magnetization decreased from 240 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (x = 0.5) to 24 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (x = 1.25).

articleTitle: Magnetization Reversal Mechanism of Co-Cr Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to investigate the mechanism of magnetization reversal in Co-Cr perpendicular recording media, the angular dependence of the hysteresis loss was investigated. For a double-layer medium consisting of a Co-Cr layer and a Permalloy backing layer, it is easy to show that rotational magnetization reversal occurs in the Co-Cr layer. Judging from both the angular dependences of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and of the hysteresis loss, the initial growth layer and the columnar structure layer in Co-Cr sputtered film were found to undergo magnetization reversal by domain wall motion and by rotation, respectively. Other Co-Cr films with different M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> values were also studied with respect to the prevailing mechanism of magnetization reversal.

articleTitle: The Characteristic Test of Dynamic Power Transmission on a Face-Type Permanent Magnet Torque Coupling
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A dynamic power transmission characteristic test was performed on a face-type magnetic coupling static power transmission system to obtain basic data on the dynamic torque of permanent magnet fragments. The test showed that coercive force was high, but careful arrangement of the magnetic poles resulted in a high transmission torque. Maximum transmission torque was obtained at the point when the magnetic shear force and magnetic repulsion force were greatest.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction of Amorphous GdFeCo Films II
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetostriction of Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-y</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub> film was measured. It was found that there was no dependence on the bias voltage. On the Gd-rich side, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> was almost constant, while on the FeCo-rich side it increased rapidly with reduction in x, reaching ten times the value on the Gd-rich side at X ≃ 11 at.%.

articleTitle: Growth and Characterization of BiGd Garnet Thick Films on 2-inch-Diameter Nd3Ga5O12 Substrates
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on the crystal quality and magneto-optical properties of 300 μm thick bismuth-substituted garnet film grown on a 2-inch diameter Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> substrate. The crystal surface of the (BiGd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (FeGaAl)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> film was specular, but one swirled section was found corresponding to a section of pits in the substrate. A correspondence of almost 1 to 1 was found between the positions of the substrate pit section and the film swirl section. Measurements of the extinction ratio showed that a uniform distribution was maintained within the specimen. Extinction ratio deterioration was found at the front of the swirls caused by the substrate pits, but no clear variation was found behind that (in the tails trailing from the pits).

articleTitle: Fundamental Behavior of Micro Gas Flow Sensor Using Magnetic Fluid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The fundamental properties of a differential voltage output type micro gas flow sensor using a magnetic fluid (MF) were studied. Gas bubbles entering the MF only pass through the upper sense coil around the MF cylinder, causing variation in the voltage generated by difference in the permeabilities of the MF and the gas. Thus the output from the differentially coupled sense coils around the MF cylinder is almost entirely due to the variation caused by the gas bubbles. This provides an extremely sensitive gas sensor in a simple configuration with superb response which is capable of detecting even a single gas bubble.

articleTitle: Properties of Amorphous Magnetic Oxides Reduced by H2
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>-CaO-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> amorphous magnetic oxides when heat-treated in an H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> atmosphere are discussed. The magnetization rose with the heat-treatment temperature and peaked at 60 emu/g at 900°C, with the CaSiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase precipitating in the neighborhood of 650°C. This magnetization increase was proportional to the applied magnetic field increase. The failure of film samples to saturate completely even at 7 kOe indicated small precipitated Fe particles and high resistivity which were measured in some samples at 0.05 ~ 0.2 μm and 4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Ω-cm, respectively.

articleTitle: Amorphous Cores Produced by High Rate Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In attempts to obtain new amorphous materials for use in magnetic cores, high-rate magnetron sputtering was used to grow Co-Zr-Mo-Ni amorphous films on glass substrates, which were annealed at temperatures above the Curie point T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> but below the crystallization temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>. Although the annealing was effective in reducing the anisotropy, it did not totally eliminate it. Ring cores with excellent frequency characteristics were also obtained.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Compound Magnetic Film with Electroplating
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Metal film was electroplated onto fine nonmagnetic wire while the latter was twisted to different angles, and then the wire was released and another film electroplated, to induce a permanent shear stress in the first layer. When symmetric and asymmetric exciting magnetic fields were applied, voltage pulses were observed to increase monotonically for symmetric driving, but an anomalous increase in positive output voltage was observed for asymmetric driving, probably due to a uniaxial anisotropy induced by the built-in shear stress.

articleTitle: Magnetic Oxide Films with Low at Valence Components in Fe-P System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The microstructure, magnetic and magneto-optical properties of Fe-p system amorphous magnetic oxide films were studied. X-ray diffraction showed clearly that the leveling off of the magnetization at 250°C after heat treatment was due to the generation of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystallization. The reduction in magnetization at about 600°C indicated that the magnetism of the films is based on the Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>. Heat treatment at 300°C increased the saturation magnetization to 1660 Gauss due to the formation of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4≪</sub> crystals. Heat treatment also increased the remanence and coercivity in the perpendicular direction to 360 Gauss and 450 Oe, respectively.

articleTitle: Magneto-Opticial Properties of Bi-Substituted GdIG Films Grown by LPE
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Reduction of optical absorption as the amount of Bi in Bi-substituted films is increased is discussed. The amount of Bi in the films grown was controlled by adjusting the supercooling temperature of the solvent, the ratio of PbO to Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> in the solvent, the substrate rotation speed and other parameters. Variation in Bi content with respect to Bi-YIG was found at substrate rotation speeds of 84 rpm and 170 rpm. The measurements of the absorption characteristics of Bi-GdIG and Bi-GdGaIG films grown on a GGG substrate indicated that they included a Bi quantity of approximately 0.8 with respect to the Bi-GdIG. A figure of merit of 6.7 deg/dB was obtained for a 21.2 μm thick Bi-GdIG film at a wavelength of 0.76 μm.

articleTitle: Noncontact Current Sensor Using an Amorphous-Core Multivibrator
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Use of a zero-magnetostriction amorphous wire two core multivibrator magnetometer in the noncontact sensing of line currents was studied. In the range ±30 percent the nonlinearity is less than 1 percent FS, indicating good linearity. The maximum value of the current to be detected can be adjusted over a wide extent by adjusting the distance between the object wire and each core. A 100 A current can be detected when the distance from the wire to the core is set to approximately 2 cm, and drift and noise are less than 0.01 percent FS.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Reconstruction by CT Technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Computer tomography techniques were used to obtain cross-sectional images of a magnetic field. A conducting wire was passed through the field at constant velocity and at a series of orientations (in 3° increments) with respect to a horseshoe magnet, and the resulting induced voltages used as projection data to extract two-dimensional tomographic images of the vertical component of the magnetic field of the magnet.

articleTitle: Plastic Flow and Field Induced Anisotropy In Co-base Amorphous Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Plastic flow, field-induced anisotropy and atomic migration in Co-base amorphous alloy films are discussed. Field-induced anisotropy is thought to be caused by atomic pairing, however it is pointed out that the increase in the atomic volume of nonmagnetic additive elements, observed in these experiments, could indicate that atomic rearrangement is suppressed and the anisotropy declines. The addition of Ta also supports this because it increases the heat stability of the permeability.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy in Columnar Structure Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A model approximating the columnar structure in Co-Cr, Co-O and other films is used to derive the resulting shape anisotropy energy K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ueff</inf>. The derived results are evaluated by comparing the predicted temperature dependence of the anisotropy energy with experimental data for Co-O films.

articleTitle: Performance Characteristics of a Bridge-Connected Magnetic Circuit in AC Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The operating characteristics under ac control of a bridge-connected magnetic circuit, consisting of an amorphous toroidal magnetic core and a U-shape core were analyzed. The centerpiece was ac-driven and the output current agreed well with the calculated current. In particular, the output current may be controlled by varying the phase angle of the ac control current in the range from O° to 180°. A theoretical analysis in some detail is presented.

articleTitle: Switching Charactersitics of (Fe, Co)-Si-B Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Variation of switching characteristics with composition in (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf> amorphous wire was studied to determine the optimal composition for use as a pulse voltage generation element. Composition was found to be optimal in the neighborhood of X = 0.5, at which a pulse value was almost 2.7 times that of Fe-based wire. Thus high magnetization is not necessarily needed to obtain a high pulse voltage.

articleTitle: Crystal Structure of Amorphous Magnetic Oxide Thin Films in Ni-Fe-P System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The crystal structure of magnetic amorphous oxide thin films in the Ni-Fe-P system made by the two source evaporation method was studied. When the amorphous thin films are heated, the magnetization disappears at the Curie temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c1</sub>), but, at almost exactly the same time, crystallization begins and causes the magnetization to once again increase. Finally the magnetization of the crystal line phase disappears at (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c2</sub>). The amorphous oxide films are presumed to possess a magnetic coupling similar to that in nickel ferrite.

articleTitle: A Tilted Sendust Sputtered Ferrite Video Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A compound magnetic head was developed by combining the high frequency magnetic characteristics of ferrite and the high B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> characteristics of sendust. Various running surface shapes were experimented with to overcome the ``wobbling'' in the read-out output frequency characteristics caused when the ferrite head tip section is within the track orbit. Placing the ferrite head tip section at the gap section edge or outside the track orbit displaced from the gap section were found to be effective measures to avoid these problems.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Al-Si Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Whereas Fe-Al-Si film of composition 5.5 percent Al-9.5 percent Si-remainder Fe (Sendust composition range) has a high permeability and good soft magnetic properties, the sensitivity of the latter to composition changes presents difficulties as regards film formation. The authors studied another promising composition range, 2.5 percent Al-5.5 percent Si-remainder Fe, sputtering films in this range on quartz substrates. Films obtained had smaller coercivities than Sendust films, near-zero magnetostriction, similar to Sendust, and a large in-plane uniaxial anisotropy. This composition borders on a disordered and an ordered phase, suggesting that film properties may be influenced greatly by annealing and other treatment.

articleTitle: Preparation of Garnet Films for Hybrid Head by RF-Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Garnet films have the low saturation flux density characteristics required for use in the ring head gap sections of hybrid heads. Conditions for preparation of garnet films by the RF sputter technique were studied. Oxygen density, annealing time, and power supplied were the most important film formation factors, while target material composition was also significant, with a critical level of 5 percent. It was found that annealing from 950°C for 30 min after film growth under 50 W applied power in an argon atmosphere including 2 percent oxygen produced the best garnet film with characteristics close to those of bulk material.

articleTitle: Metallic Thin Film Media for Hard Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The demand for high density magnetic disk drives is increasing. Thin film media, such as plated disks, sputtered metallic disks and sputtered ferrite disks, have been developed for use as such high density recording media. The technology developed for plated disks and sputtered metallic disks is outlined. Production processes, magnetic properties, reliability and high density recording characteristics of these disks are discussed. The advantages and potential of such media for recording at higher densities are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Particulate Medium Oriented Longitudinally Inside and Perpendicularly at Surface
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This report takes another look at the VAST (Vertical magnetic orientation-AC demagnetization-Smoothing period-sequential Train) technique used to fabricate double-layer particulate media oriented longitudinally inside and perpendicularly at the surface from CrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> particles and nitrocellulose with a urethane binder. Infrared irradiation was performed to evaporate the solvent instead of natural evaporation to improve the viscosity of the surface perpendicular oriented layer, and to ensure a controlled thin, uniform thickness surface layer.

articleTitle: Aging Properties of Amorphous GdTbFeCo Magnetic Films and the Effect of Other Elements Added to Them
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Tests on adding B, Bi, Al, Cr, Sm, and Cu to GdTbFeCo amorphous films revealed that B tends to reduce film deterioration and the Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>). Cu or small amounts of Sm lowered the amount of coercive force (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) deterioration, but θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> showed no substantial change. Cr had a larger effect than Sm, and also exhibited the smallest decrease in θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> (to 73 percent of the original value after 100 h). The addition of Cr also lowered the Curie temperature as much as 70°C at 3.6 area%.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Compositionally Modulated Nd-Co Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A series of compositionally modulated Nd-Co thin films was prepared by UHV evaporation. The modulated structure and composition of the films were studied by X-ray diffraction measurement and energy-dispersive X-ray microanalysis, respectively. Magnetization and anisotropy measurements were carried out using a vibrating sample magnetometer in the temperature range between 77 K and room temperature. A coherent structure was found over the modulation length Λ (20 Å ≤ Λ ≤ 70 Å). The magnetization of films with an atomic ratio of Nd:Co = 1:3 changed slightly with Λ, but the perpendicular anisotropy energy decreased significantly with increasing Λ. The reduction of the anisotropy energy seems to be due to a decrease in the proportion of atoms which are adjacent to the interfaces between Nd and Co layers.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of Magnetic Sensor for Nondestructive Test
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Computer simulations of flaw detection by a differential transformer type magnetic sensor are described. To enable treatment of the relative motion between sensor and test piece, a boundary element method was adopted in place of the usual finite element method of analysis. The results of an analysis assuming a sensor running over an iron bar with a buried flaw are presented.

articleTitle: Reduction of Optical Absorption in Bi-Substituted Garnet Film by Annealing
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: LPE film was grown using Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> single flux to realize the high Faraday rotation and low absorption provided by high density Bi-substitution required of material used for 0.8 μm optical isolators. The melt from Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> single flux does not contain bivalent ions such as Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, so Pt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup> taken into the film or oxygen vacancies occurring within the film generate Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, and increase optical absorption at 0.8 μm. Generation of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> was prevented by adding bivalent ions, like Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, in the melt, and optical absorption declined. This paper reports the results of investigations in which in addition to adding bivalent ions, annealing was used successfully to reduce Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and optical absorption. Investigation of the relation between the effect of oxygen partial pressure during annealing and annealing temperature established that the equilibrium oxygen partial pressure and reaction rate differ with the electrical type of the film.

articleTitle: Microscopic Structure and Magnetic Properties in State of FeMn Alloy Added Bi
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-Mn-Bi films were formed by electron beam vacuum evaporation, and then oxidized by annealing in an oxygen atmosphere to obtain ferromagnetic oxide films. The film composition profiles and magnetic properties were then investigated. Depth profiles as determined by AES indicated a uniform film composition, but X-ray diffraction indicated the formation of FeMnBiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> upon annealing. From the annealing temperature dependences of the saturated magnetization and coercive force, a magnetic transformation point exists near 300°C, a result confirmed by separate resistivity measurements.

articleTitle: Investigation of Characteristics for a Plane-Anisotropic Mn-Al-C Permanent Magnet on Multi-Pole Magnetization
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multiple pole magnetization of Mn-Al-C permanent magnets was studied experimentally and in FEM calculations. The cases of 8, 24- and 48-pole magnetization were treated, and flux densities determined by Hall probe measurements. Calculations agreed well with measured values, which indicated that fairly strong surface flux densities can be achieved even for larger numbers of magnetic poles.

articleTitle: Effective Permeability of CoNbZr Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of substrate temperature, magnetic fields, heat treatment, and film thickness on permeability is discussed. The authors obtained good soft magnetic characteristics with uniaxial heat treatment up to 200°C, and learned that in-plane anisotropy can be controlled by applying a magnetic field of several Oe while heat treating. A magnetic field applied during sputtering can cause the easy axis to change at different temperatures and in different temperature ranges. Films thicker than 0.4 μm had a nearly constant permeability, but the permeability of those thinner than that was diminished.

articleTitle: FMR in Co-Cr Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To clarify the mechanism of magnetization reversal in Co-Cr perpendicular magnetization films, the authors studied ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) in the X-band (9.27 GHz) in films of various thicknesses. X-band FMR absorption under a field applied perpendicular to the film was attributed to the appearance of reverse domains in films; and FMR absorption under a parallel field in 0.02 μm thick film is believed to occur as a result of the prevailing demagnetization factor.

articleTitle: Crystal Orientation and Magneto-Optical properties of Co-Ferrite Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between Co-ferrite film orientation and film growth conditions was investigated. Varying the sputter conditions in the initial growth period make it possible to produce a film with a [100] dominant azimuth perpendicular to the film surface. The [100]-oriented film could not be obtained without an initial layer, demonstrating that the initial layer plays a very important role in film orientation.

articleTitle: Preparation and Characteristics of Cloth Inductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A cloth inductor consisting of mechanically interwoven amorphous ferromagnetic fibers and conducting fibers is described, and the inductor characteristics reported for various fiber lengths, diameters, and weaving patterns. The inductance L increases nearly in proportion to the fiber length, and in proportion to the second power of the amorphous fiber diameter and the second power of the number of conducting fiber turns per unit length, as expected. The leakage flux and total inductance also depend on the relative flux orientations of neighboring amorphous fibers.

articleTitle: Fundamental Behavior of Ternary Pulse Output Type FOC
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization curve of a Ferrite Orthogonal Core (FOC) with excellent squareness ratio when the flux is controlled was studied for a new A/D conversion function. It was demonstrated that the FOC output voltage could be processed as a ternary digital output, and plotting the relation between the period intervals of two pulses of the same polarity, of a positive and a negative pulse, and the control magnetomotive force showed that phase control of the pulses is possible.

articleTitle: Hybrid Heads and Recording Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A hybrid head employing a high saturation flux density material on one gap surface and low saturation flux density material on the other was studied. Compared with the values for normal heads, the hybrid head had about 1.4 times the value of the maximum magnetization gradient on the recording media and its magnetization gradient half-width was significantly less. These results show that it is reasonable to expect that the output and recording density of the hybrid head would be improved over those of normal heads, making it very suitable for the high density required for digital recording.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Effect of Invar Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Whereas an fcc structure has been reported for vacuum evaporated FeNi thin films, magnetostriction and other effects may result in precipitation of other phases. To study local phase precipitation in such thin films, measurements of the magneto-optical effect, the Hall effect, ferromagnetic resonance absorption spectra, and other magnetic properties were performed. The Kerr rotation angle was found to vary more smoothly with composition than did M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. From ferromagnetic resonance absorption results, films under 500 Å thick tended to have inhomogeneous structures, with much local phase precipitation.

articleTitle: Read After Write Characteristics of Probe-Type Thin Film Head for Perpendicular Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of write and read characteristics on the spacing for a probe-type head/double-layer perpendicular magnetic recording media system and for a ring head/single-layer perpendicular media system was measured. Write efficiency for the probe-type head/double-layer film system was five times that of the ring head/single-layer film system, and output for the latter was approximately 1/10 that of the former. Thus the probe-type head/double-layer film media system has good read after write efficiency and its spacing loss is small, confirming that it is a good arrangement for application to rigid disk devices.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistive Sensors Using Ni-Co Films with Auxiliary Pole of Ni-Fe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors studied the magnetoresistive effect, effective anisotropy field, domain patterns and reading abilities of an improved sensor structure made of highly magnetoresistive Ni-Co films with an auxiliary Ni-Fe film pole. The demagnetizing field in the improved sensors having the same Ni-Co stripe width as conventional sensors was reduced to half that of the latter. With angular changes in applied field or application of low bias fields, the magnetoresistive effect in conventional sensors was weakened due to the existence of domain walls. The improved sensors, on the other hand, consist of a single domain; thus the magnetoresistive effect is not decreased under the same field conditions. The read output using the magnetoresistive effect of the improved sensors is roughly 1.6 to 1.8 times greater than for conventional sensors. The ratio of the stripe width of the sensors to the recording bit length was found to be an important factor in enabling greater distances from medium to sensor.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Co-Substituted LPE Magnetic Garnet Films at 1.54 μm
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co-substituted magnetic garnet (YNd)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (CoGeFe)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> thin films were grown by LPE on GGG {111} substrates with the aim of maximizing the magneto-optical properties at 1.5 μm, where absorption loss of optical fibers is minimal. θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> and γ were found to increase as Co content increases. The variation in refractive index (n) at 1.54 μm was much more rapid than at 1.15 μm. Since the value of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> at 1.15 μm does not depend on the Co content, it was concluded that reduction in n at 1.15 μm was mainly due to reduction in iron ions. A maximum TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>-TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> mode conversion efficiency (F) of 50 percent was obtained at 1.54 μm. This maximum seems to be due to the θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> maximum at 1.54 μm which occurs with Co-substitution. It is to be expected that optimizing birefringence will improve the value of F.

articleTitle: Output Characteristics of the Compound Magnetic Sensitive Element in the Disturbed Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To study the stability of magnetically sensitive Vicalloy wire, which when properly stressed consists of core and peripheral regions with different coercivities, the authors twisted wire samples to varying degrees, magnetized the samples, and applied a disturbing magnetic field. The magnetized state of the peripheral regions of samples were highly stable against such external disturbances, and in particular no evidence of creep or similar phenomena was observed.

articleTitle: Integration of Garnet Films by Using Laser Etching Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new four-stage technique for integrating multiple iron garnet films on a single substrate is presented. A film is first grown on a GGG substrate by LPE. Ar ion laser etching is used in the second stage to remove a section of this film. Etching terminates automatically at the film-substrate interface. A second film is grown following the contours of the first by hetero-epitaxy in the third stage. The resulting film is flattened in the final stage by laser etching with the substrate and layered film immersed in phosphoric acid. This technique seems promising for realizing a wide variety of highly functional and compact integrated garnet film devices.

articleTitle: Comparison of Magnetic Properties Between Sputtered Co-Cr and Fe-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To study the origin of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, the authors compare the magnetic properties of sputtered Co-Cr and Fe-Cr films. In the latter, it is concluded that Cr-poor bcc phase is precipitated in a Cr-rich (53 at% Cr) phase, and that the magnetic anisotropy is due to the shape anisotropy of precipitated Fe grains. As for Co-Cr films, the M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>-T curves and other results suggest considerable composition variation in hcp single-phase regions.

articleTitle: Bi-Substituted Garnet Films For Magneto-Optic Memory -Sputter Opposition In Ar-H2 Gas-
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between film characteristics and oxygen deficits was investigated. The amount of Bi in the film drastically decreased with increase in the amount of hydrogen. This may be due to the weakness of the Bi affinity to oxygen. The X-ray diffraction intensity of film produced by introducing hydrogen at 5% of Ar is significantly weaker than that for film grown in pure Ar. Film grown in Ar + H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> showed improved optical homogeneity at the crystal grain boundaries resulting in large reduction in light intensity variation coming close to that of the amorphous film.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Co Thin Films Deposited by Ion Beam Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-Co thin films were formed on slide glass by ion beam sputtering, and their magnetic properties were investigated for various compositions, substrate temperatures and annealing conditions. The bcc structure films deposited at low temperatures received a compressive stress from substrates, which decreased and changed to a tensile stress as the substrate temperature was raised, caused by accelerated crystal grain growth. Large saturation magnetizations, in excess of 20 kG, were obtained. However, films formed on unheated substrates have considerable H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k⊥</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> values, which decreased as the substrate temperature increased. Vacuum annealing had an effect similar to that of substrate heating. It seems that the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy energy is mainly caused by the stress induced magnetic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy in Fe-(3 ˜ 4 wt%) Al-(5 ˜ 6 wt%≫)Si Alloy Single Crystal
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The behavior of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> of Fe-Al-Si single crystal was investigated for the cause of soft magnetism in this composition. Measurement of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> variation with temperature for a sample annealed from 1200°C revealed that K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> does not change sign. Measurement of the change in saturation magnetism with temperature over the -200 to 800°C temperature range supported the view that the samples measured in this experiment were single-phase DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. The results did not conflict with the steady state diagram analogy.

articleTitle: Rolled Grain Texture of Rapidly Quenched Silicon Steel
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The variation in grain texture with rolling and annealing in relatively thick rapidly quenched ribbon was studied. It was found that (110) recrystallized grains produced by secondary recrystallization begin to grow near 1000°C, and with a temperature increase of less than 50 degrees more, there is about 90 percent (110) recrystallized grain. Grain diameter also increases rapidly with recrystallization to an average of between 3 and 4 mm.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Effects of Tetrahedrally Coordinated Co2+ in Ferrites
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A large magneto-optical effect near the wavelengths of 0.7 μm and 1.5 μm in ferrites containing tetrahedral Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions was studied on the basis of the crystal field theory. The spectrum calculated essentially reproduced the experimentally observed Faraday rotation curves of the Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ion-substituted ferrites. Eigenstates corresponding to the 0.7 μm and 1.5 μm transitions were determined in the framework of the strong crystal field approximation using data from the absorption spectra of the tetrahedral Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions in the garnets. The strengths of these transitions and the spin-orbit interaction coefficients of the excited state are calculated from the eigenstates. The Faraday rotation spectrum was calculated with these parameters in the wavelength range of 0.5 μm to 2.0 μm.

articleTitle: Simple Laser-Light Modulator with Acrylic Plate Faraday Rotator for Educational Use
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: He-Ne and other gas lasers, which were once expected to become the major tools of optical communications in the future, now seem to be very far from practical application in communications technology. But the beauty and excellent rectilinear propagation of a gas laser is very moving, and it is still attractive as an educational material in optical communications. The author constructed a simple optical communication system using a He-Ne gas laser for educational use. In this system, a commercially available acryl plate (cut to square bar, 10 × 10 × 20 mm in size) was used as the Faraday rotator to modulate the laser beam, because it is easy to process, highly transparent, lightweight, and easy to obtain.

articleTitle: Rotary Encoder Using Amorphous Star-Shaped Core Field Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors describe a magnetic rotary encoder consisting of a ring-shaped multi-pole magnet and amorphous magnetic core multivibrator sensors positioned radially around the magnet. The frequency-modulated output is sinusoidal, with a distortion of less than 1% when operating at 50 kHz; the encoder is impervious to mechanical disturbances, and can be used at relatively high temperatures.

articleTitle: Faraday Rotation of Co-Ferrite Thin Films Prepared by Single Source Evaporation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-Co alloy film was oxidized to produce a transparent cobalt ferrite film. The amount of Faraday rotation was measured as a function of the quantity of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, which was increased and decreased by reduction and oxidation. In the film reduced to increase the amount of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, the Faraday rotation curve becomes positive. The absorption coefficient increases with increase in Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>. When the film is oxidized at 600°C, the Faraday rotation curve becomes negative again and the absorption coefficient decreases.

articleTitle: Influence of H2 Partial Pressure on Sputtered TbFeCo Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> partial pressure on TbFeCo films was studied and it was found that increasing the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> partial pressure lowers both H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> (changing the magnetic anisotropy from perpendicular to in-plane), and the film deposition rate, while increasing Ms to a value approaching that of FeCo films. The various ion currents in the plasma increased until the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> partial pressure reached 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> torr and this agreed with changes in the film deposition rate.

articleTitle: Effect of High Permeability Film in Magneto-Optical Readout Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new type of magnetic head, called a domain-modulation type optical reproduction head, which uses a magneto-optical effect for signal reproduction, is proposed. The prototype head consists of a high-permeability magnetic film and a magnetic garnet film with a reflex mirror. The high-permeability magnetic film works as a magnetic flux guide to transfer the fringing magnetic flux from the recorded bits in the magnetic recording medium to a magnetic garnet film, and modulates the width of the magnetic domains sufficiently to enable reproduction by a laser beam. Thus high-resolution reproduction with regard to both track density and bit density is anticipated. To investigate the feasibility of use of such a head, a prototype head was placed on recorded magnetic tape, and the modulated domains in the magnetic garnet film were observed through a polarization microscope. We found that the change in domain width reached values greater than 1 μm for magnetic garnet film with a natural domain width of 2.5 μm. According to an analytical reproduction model, this value is sufficient to enable a high signal-to-noise ratio (of approximately 75 dB) in reproducing recorded bits by a 2-μm laser beam.

articleTitle: U-Type Target for High Rate Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new type of sputtering target, which produces magnetic fields strong enough for magnetron sputtering of ferromagnetic targets, and a high concentration of particle beams was developed. The prototype target is a U-shaped target, but with no target material on the bottom of the "U". In experiments, a uniform 130 Oe field was applied from the sides of the target with an electromagnet. The measured angular distribution of sputtered particles suggested that some particles come from the bottom of the "U" which is covered by the material sputtered Å from both sides of the "U". At an Ar pressure of 6 mtorr and power input of 1 A and 640 V, deposition rates of up to 1500 Å/min were obtained.

articleTitle: Bit Shift Characteristics on Perpendicular Recording Using Single-Layer Co-Cr Media and Ring Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Bit shift characteristics are important parameters for perpendicular recording by ring heads on single-layer Co-Cr media. Bit shift dependences on media characteristics are studied experimentally. A simulation model of recorded magnetization transitions is presented to clarify the dependences under the following assumptions: 1) Media magnetization has a perpendicular component only and is constant through the thickness. 2) Media hysteresis is given by a rectangular loop, determined by H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> with no minor loop.
