It was found that bit shift differs only slightly with media thickness, and for a given bit shift, high recording density is obtained with low H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> media.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Magnetic Recording Media Noise
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The noise properties of magnetic recording media partly depend on the type of medium, i.e., whether the medium is of the magnetic thin film type or the particulate type. In magnetic thin film media, such as Co-Ni-P plated disks, the lowest noise level is that of dc-erased noise, and when signals are recorded after dc-erasure the level of the modulation noise increases gradually as the recording wavelength is shortened, until it reaches a maximum level at a certain wavelength. On the other hand, in particulate media, the noise level is highest for modulation noise, followed in turn by dc-erased noise and ac-erased noise. In the analysis described in this paper, the irregular fluctuations in the direction of magnetization and the number of magnetic particles per unit volume have been taken into account, and the results of the analysis make it clear that the relative noise level of the ac-erased, dc-erased, and modulation noise depends on these fluctuations.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of ME-Tapes with Narrow-Gap MonocrystallineF errite Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The high-density magnetic recording characteristics of CoNi evaporated tapes with a monocrystalline ferrite narrow-gap head are investigated by comparison with recording using a sendust head. An output of close to 200 kFRPI for recording/reproduction by the ferrite head was found for one of the tape samples, closely approaching the value for sendust head recording. This suggests that improving the magnetic properties of tapes will make it possible to increase the output at high-density for the ferrite head at recording/reproduction.

articleTitle: Power Magnetics and Creative Power
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan

articleTitle: Iron Loss of Silicon Steel Under Square Wave Voltage Excitation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The iron loss characteristics of silicon steel were studied using the iron loss estimation method previously proposed by the authors. The rate of increase of the square wave iron loss with respect to the sine wave iron loss was only slightly greater than predicted. It was found that this iron loss estimation method provides adequate precision for widespread application to excitation due to square wave voltages, such as occur in inverter transformers.

articleTitle: Iron Oxide Sputtered Films with Perpendicular Anisotropy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Perpendicular magnetized sputtered iron oxide film was fabricated. At a substrate temperature of 205°C, the sputtered film was in-plane magnetized, but perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was induced at 176°C. A perpendicular magnetized film was obtained at an oxygen partial pressure of 0.18mTorr over a rather wide substrate temperature range. In the x-ray diffraction pattern there were several unclear Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> peaks which could not be precisely determined.

articleTitle: Effects of Plasma Exposure on Magnetization of Ion-implanted Bubble Garnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Exposure to plasma results in an increase in the change in induced anisotropy field ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> of ion-implanted garnet film. In this work, the change in saturation magnetization was also studied. Ne<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions were implanted into (YSmLuCa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (GeFe)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> film and then exposed to plasma. Whereas a linear decrease in saturation magnetization 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> with implantation dose was seen, plasma exposure caused an increase which was also proportional to the dose. The temperature dependence of 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> indicated that plasma exposure raised the T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, which had fallen from 246°C to 180°C with implantation, back to 198°C. Occlusion of hydrogen in the plasma may be partially responsible for this behavior.

articleTitle: Ferrite Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors describe a method of temperature compensation in a sensor, consisting of stimulation and search coils, for use in unmanned transport systems. By choosing an operating frequency such that the temperature dependent of the two types of coils cancel each other, fluctuations in the sensor output in the temperature range -10 to 50°C were suppressed to within 10%.

articleTitle: Torque Sensor Using Amorphous Star-Shaped Core Magnetic Field Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for measuring the torque exerted on an induction motor shaft by detecting differences in the shaft angles of twist is reported. A pair of precise twist angle sensors, consisting of multiple pole magnet rings surrounded by radial arrays of amorphous magnetic core field-sensitive elements, with their outputs 90° out of phase, are used to detect the angle of twisting of the shaft, from which the torque is determined. The sensor output was found to be highly linear with respect to the actual torque.

articleTitle: Overview of Metallic Superlattice Studies
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Recent developments in metallic superlattice studies are surveyed and some perspectives are presented. Especially the possibility of preparing magnetic monolayer systems is discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Y-RE-Fe Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors substituted Y for the rare-earth (RE) element in RE-TM films and studied the changes in the anisotropy of the RE atoms and the magnetic characteristics of the films. Gd substituted for Y tended to increase M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>. All of the films studied had amorphous macroscopic structures as determined by X-ray analysis.

articleTitle: Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy in Fe(5~6 wt%)-Si(3~4 wt%)-Al Alloy Single Crystals
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Temperature dependence of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant, K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, and the magnetostriction constants, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</sub> and λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub>, were determined for alloy single crystals containing 4.8 wt% Si, 5.0 wt% Al, bal Fe and 4.7 wt% Si, 3.8 wt% Al, bal Fe. The temperature dependence and magnitude of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> for the two alloys were found to be completely different: K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> = 9.1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for the former, and 1.1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for the latter alloy, both at room temperature. The values of λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</sub> and λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub> (× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>) at room temperature were found to be 4.8 and 9.8 for the former, and 7.8 and 5.7 for the latter alloy. A unique diffraction line, due to the existence of a DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> type ordered structure, was clearly observed for both alloys. From the results obtained, the following were concluded: 1) a discrete change in the values of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> occurs at the phase boundary between the α and the α + DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phases; 2) the magnitude of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> for the alloy samples consisting of the DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> ordered phase is smaller than that for the &3x003B1; + DO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> phase.

articleTitle: The Effects of Sm on Amorphous Gd-Fe Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Sm was added to GdFe films to make GdSmFe amorphous films and their magnetic characteristics were studied. It was found that GdSmFe films with quality equal to TbFe films could be produced. This indicates that GdSmFe could be viable as a magneto-optical medium.

abstract: This index covers all items.papers, correspondence, reviews, etc..that appeared in this periodical during 1987. Note that Vol. TJMJ-1 was dated 1985, and no issues were published dated 1986. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name, and cross-references from all coauthors. The Subject Index contains several entries for each item under appropriate subject headings, and subject cross-references. It is always necessary to refer to the primary entry in the Author Index for the exact title, coauthors, and comments/corrections.

articleTitle: Micro-Kerr Loops of CoZr Stripe Pattern
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: M-H loops were measured at different points in Co-Zr stripes of varying widths (W = 20 to 100 μm) using micro-Kerr effect measuring equipment. The M-H loops obtained were biased with respect to the applied field when W ≤ 50 μm, and the rising and falling edges of loops were partially inverted when W ≥ 70 μm. Loops were used to compute the number of magnetic domains, and fair agreement with Bitter domain observations was obtained, indicating that domain information can be obtained by this method without sample contamination, as in the Bitter method.

articleTitle: Preparation of Magneto-Optical Disks Using RE-TM Alloy Targets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of two very common targets (TbFeCo and TbCo alloys) were evaluated and it was learned that sputtering such alloy targets varies the sample composition, but target oxygen content has no effect on the magnetic characteristics.

articleTitle: Relation between Signal Quality and Groove Shape in Magneto-Optical Disk(1)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of groove shape on recording media was measured with a static measurement system developed by the authors to investigate media magneto-optic characteristics in the microscopic range. Reflectivity decreased as the depth of the groove increased due to the groove diffraction effect. Decrease in reflectivity also seemed to be the cause of reduction in the rotation angle. The coercive force only reached a critical variation point when the groove was shallow, which seemed to be because grooves deeper than the 20nm film thickness of the experimental samples divided the media in two.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of a-CoNbTi/SiO2 Layered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of multilayering on the soft magnetic characteristics of a-CoNbTi/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> amorphous alloy layered films were studied. H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of a single-layer film increased rapidly as film thickness decreased from 300 Å, but H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> decreased by multilayering a-CoNbTi with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thin layers. Favorable ac characteristics were, however, not obtained when the magnetization measurement direction was parallel to the internal magnetization. Thus, a perpendicular field annealing was needed. The magnetic layers were less than 2500 Å thick, the thinner the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and magnetic layers, the higher was the maximum permeability.

articleTitle: Operation of High-Frequency Half-Wave Rectifier Circuit Which Contains Saturable Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Design and operation of an amorphous spike-reduction saturable core used in a half wave rectifier circuit was studied in the high-frequency waveband of a 100 kHz operating frequency. It was found that the reverse current flowing through the circuit is controlled by the core exciting current, and that the core absorbs the spike and is reset. Reset flux was also found resulting in extremely low reduction in forward direction load current due to the flyback flux. However it was established that it is possible to determine the number of turns of the core coil to achieve the desired spike reduction.

articleTitle: Experimental Considerations on Photovoltaic Power System Using Orthogonal-Core-Type DC-AC Converter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Operation characteristics of a photovoltaic power system using an orthogonal-core type dc-ac converter linking a solar array and pre-existing ac system were studied. The link was established at about 20 percent sunlight, and as the sunlight increases, the power supplied from the solar array to the ac system increases as anticipated. Favorable operating characteristics were found even when sunlight varied irregularly.

articleTitle: Pressure Dependence of Disaccommodation in Ni-Zn Ferrite with Co Impurity
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The initial permeability decay, which is caused by disaccommodation in a polycrystalline Ni-Zn ferrite sample, was measured in a -60 ~ -40°C range under hydrostatic pressure of 1 bar to 2.5 kbar. The results were analyzed using a Richter-type relaxation hypothesis. The temperature dependence study of the upper limit T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> of the relaxation time spectrum gave the activation energy of 0.58 eV. The activation volume determined from the pressure dependence of T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was found to be dependent on temperature and its size had an order of magnitude of 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/mol. These results are compatible with the view that the observed disaccommodation is caused by ionic diffusion, in spite of the widely accepted view that it is due to electron diffusion in this material. From these results, the ionic diffusion model seems to be more favorable than the widely accepted electron diffusion model.

articleTitle: Mechanocardiograph Sensors Using Amorphous Star-Shaped Core Multivibrators
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Highly stable and accurate mechanocardiograph sensors are presented using linear magnet-displacement sensors with a star-shaped amorphous core multivibrator. 2N zero-magnetostrictive amorphous wire cores are combined in a new star-shape configuration, in which the influence of external disturbance fields such as terrestrial fields is almost completely eliminated and the signal field generated by a small magnet is stably detected. These linear displacement sensors can detect the displacement of a magnet through about 3 mm with a drift of less than 0.2 μm. Mechanocardiographs of a heartbeat, a phonocardiograph, and blood-vessel pulsation are stably and easily detected by fixing a small magnet on the chest wall or the blood-vessel position, combined with a non-contact type displacement sensor.

articleTitle: Orthorhombic Magnetic Anisotropy in (EuBi)3Fe5O12 Garnet (110) Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of LPE growth conditions on Bi substitution and the previously reported large orthorhombic magnetic anisotropy in (EuBi)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> films are described. The results, with the anisotropy expressed in terms of Gyorgy's parameters A and B, indicated that R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> (= Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Eu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (= PbO/B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) do not have so great an effect on the amount of Bi substitution as was previously believed, nor do they greatly influence the magnetic anisotropy. The growth temperature essentially determines the Bi substitution and resulting lattice mismatch.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Mn-Sb Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Mn-Sb multilayered films were prepared by the alternate vapor deposition method. MnSb is formed even at a substrate temperature of -100°C, demonstrating the extreme reactivity of Mn. A perfectly uniform ferromagnetic MnSb polycrystal was obtained when the Mn to Sb mole ratio was 1 : 1. When MnSb was in the equilibrium state, the most Sb-rich MnSb system compound was produced, and the reaction between Mn and Sb did not proceed beyond that point, demonstrating that it is possible to fabricate a multilayered film with a ferromagnetic ultrathin MnSb film sandwiched between Sb layers.

articleTitle: A Contact Type Amorphous Torque Sensor with Wide Dynamic Range
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A torque sensor with a broad dynamic range employing amorphous ribbons in contact with a sensor head is described. A uniaxial anisotropy was induced in the FeCoSiB amorphous ribbons by magnetic field annealing. Ribbons with various K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">uo</sub>/λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> used. As expected, a larger K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">uo</sub>/λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> resulted in a broader dynamic range, but with lowered sensitivity. In stationary torque detection experiments, a sensitivity about 10 times that possible using strain gauges was achieved at a dynamic range of 2000 μST.

articleTitle: Multilayered Structures and Magnetic Properties of Fe-Si-Ru Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for controlling the domain structure by improving the multilayerization of Fe-Si-Ru alloy, Ni-Fe alloy and SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to improve the reproduction sensitivity of single-pole perpendicular magnetic heads. Measurements of the permeability of the Fe-Si-Ru multilayered film before and after patterning revealed that before patterning it was almost constant at 2200 up to an intermediate SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer thickness of 30 nm, and that it decreased above that point, but after patterning, the permeability improved as the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer thickness increased and reached a maximum of 1000 at 20 nm.

articleTitle: Development of a 3.5-Inch High-Speed and High-Capacity FDD
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan

articleTitle: Physical Considerations on Shearing of M-H Curve
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The author discusses the discontinuous jump in the M-H curve of a magnetic body in the limit as its length is reduced toward zero, and notes that the demagnetizing field is not a useful concept in explaining this discontinuity. This stems from the tendency to ignore the limits to application of the vector magnetization M as a vector sum of magnetic moments which are located at different points in space.

articleTitle: Noncontact Torque Sensor Using Magnetic Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A noncontact torque sensor based on magnetic heads positioned at 45° to the shaft was studied. Plotting the static torque detection characteristics for various ribbon-head spacings showed that for spacings of from 0.5 to 0.7 mm, the characteristics do not change much. The zero-point variations for spacings from 0.2 to 0.7 mm were under 0.7 mV. A driving frequency ω/2π = 312 kHz was employed to minimize the effect of the ferromagnetic shaft. When a large shaft is used making the sensor configuration proportionately larger may result in a spacing of several mm.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of Amorphous TbFeCoBi Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Bi was added to TbFeCo and its effects on the TM sublattice magnetization (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sub>) were studied. The Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) was low at all Co concentrations. The addition of Bi increases μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sub>, but has comparatively little effect on M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sub>. Bi increases θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> in Gd-TM films, but decreases θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> in Tb-TM films. This can be attributed to RE-Bi interactions. When both Tb and Gd were used (TbGdFeCoBi films), increasing the amount of Gd made θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> rise at three times the rate of increase in TbGdFeCo films.

articleTitle: High-density Information Storage by Means of Magnetic Holography on Amorphous TbFe Thin Films (II)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The recording characteristics and hologram patterns of data storage by magnetic holography are described in detail. When the reconstruction was like a spatially filtered image of the original pattern, it was observed that the middle part of the contour of each character of the original pattern was saturated by the excess intensity of the object beam. It was found that the recording margin in magnetic holography is very small, and is strongly affected by the original data pattern. Adjustment of intensity of the object and reference beams at the recording stage is thus very important.

articleTitle: Forced Magnetostriction in Amorphous Gd-Fe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between forced magnetostriction in amorphous Gd-Fe films and film composition was studied. It was discovered that the forced magnetostriction previously considered to be small enough to ignore is actually too large to ignore. The forced magnetostriction exhibits a significant dependence on film composition suggesting that it is strongly related to the Fe moment in the film. It was also confirmed that Gd-Fe film forced magnetostriction is dependent on temperature.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Properties of Bi-Substituted Magnetic Garnets and Their Application to a Long Wavelength Optical Isolator
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: GdBiIG Faraday rotator magneto-optical characteristics measurements showed that the 1.3 μm linear polarized light transmitted through a Faraday rotator coated with a nonreflective coating decreases at extinction, but increases at transmission as the applied magnetic field increases. Using this and other results, the authors constructed a 1.3 μm optical isolator using a GdBiIG Faraday rotator. Calcite birefringent plates were used for the polarizer and the analyzer. A cylindrical permanent magnet was included to bring the Faraday rotator to saturation magnetization. The GdBiIG Faraday rotator loss was 0.04 dB, and the combined loss for the polarizer and the analyzer was 0.05 dB, for a total loss of 0.09 dB; an extremely low value. The level of 1.3 μm linear polarized light transmitted through the Faraday rotator coated with a nonreflective coating was measured by rotating the analyzer.

articleTitle: A Numerical Method for Estimation of Core Characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for estimating the characteristics of magnetic cores with gaps in the magnetic circuits was studied to aid in the design of electrical equipment based on such cores. The eddy current effect in a core was considered from the point of view of classical theory, while the tableau equation was obtained by applying the tableau method to the circuit. Expected values for the measurable circuit variables are given by the periodic solutions of the tableau equation, and these can be used to investigate the ratios of hysteresis loss and eddy current loss, very difficult in a measurement.

articleTitle: Growth Induced Magnetic Anisotropy of Co-Substituted LPE Magnetic Garnet Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors succeed in quantitatively explaining the uniaxial magnetic anisotropy of Co-substituted liquid-phase epitaxy (LPE) garnet films with an a-site Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> nonuniform distribution model. They also demonstrate that this anisotropy is induced by irregular Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> distribution during the growth process. A-site Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> makes a positive contribution to K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and a negative one to K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, while d-site Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> makes a negative contribution to K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and has no effect on K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Using ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) to determine the crystalline anisotropy constants K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and the uniaxial anisotropy constants K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</inf>, the authors determined that a-site Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> makes a dominant contribution. A-site can be further divided into four a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> -sites. When Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> is evenly distributed to each of these a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> -sites, then Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> contributes to K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, but while unevenly distributed at a single a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> -site, it induces positive K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</inf>. When Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> is found at every a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> -site, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</inf> decreases and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> increases. The predicted values were supported by experimental results.

articleTitle: Disaccommodation of Permeability on CoZrNb Amorphous Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The deterioration of the permeability of CoZrNb amorphous films is discussed. The permeability was measured using a B-H loop tracer, and the deterioration with heat treatment or aging in ac magnetic fields. Deterioration is more pronounced in thinner films, but no deterioration was observed in samples aged in ac magnetic fields. Permeability was restored by reheating, but began to deteriorate afterward. The degree of deterioration also depends on the film composition. The results indicated that the deterioration was caused by atomic rearrangement near the film and substrate interface.

articleTitle: Angular Dependence of Coercivity for Barium Ferrite Coated Perpendicular Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors studied the angular dependences of the coercivity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and remanent coercivity rH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> in Ba-ferrite perpendicular-oriented film and other media, to investigate magnetization reversal in Ba-ferrite particles in the media. Comparisons with behaviors predicted by the Stoner-Wohlfarth coherent rotation model indicated that while magnetization reversal in such film shows single-domain behavior, it cannot be regarded as necessarily coherent in nature, although reversals within individual particles may be so.

articleTitle: Reduction of Growth Rate in Bi-Substituted Bubble Garnets Using MoO3-added Melt
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It was found that by adding MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> to the PbO-Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> flux used in LPE growth of Bi-substituted garnet films, the growth rate can be reduced, facilitating control over the film growth process. The ratio of Mo to Pb in the melt was varied, and the effects on the growth rate Gr, the lattice mismatch Δa<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>, the anisotropy energy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>, the saturation induction 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, and the Curie temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, were observed. Changes in film properties can be compensated by small adjustments in the melt composition.

articleTitle: The New Unified Framework in Physics and the Research in Magnetics II, The Hyperfine Magnetic Field at the Electron and the Magneto-Optic Effects
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The author discusses various implications for magnetics of the new framework which unites classical and quantum physics. For instance, it is noted that, in conventional physics, the magnetic interaction which must occur between electrons represented as current vortex rings has been ignored, and that this interaction, together with the requirement for the absence of singularities in electron wave functions, leads to the Pauli principle. Elsewhere, the author notes that Larmor precession about a hyperfine magnetic field may contribute to the Faraday rotation effect.

articleTitle: Barkhausen Noise in Yoke Type MR Heads (II)-Inverse Effect of Magnetostriction
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan

articleTitle: Decay Characteristics of Electromagnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The decay characteristics following dc magnetization of a solenoid valve were studied, with one pole, a movable iron piece, covered with either chrome plating or foil. The range of chrome plating thicknesses affecting the time constants was extremely small, under 10 μm in these experiments. Two types of behavior were observed depending on the spring force and the excitation current. One characterized by stable separation times and the other by a rapid increasing separation time.

articleTitle: Magnetic Characteristics of Amorphous GdTbCoFe Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The temperature dependence of the coercive force (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) and the saturation magnetization (M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) of GdTbCoFe quaternary amorphous films was studied. As the Co ratio in the transition metals (TM) increases, both the slope of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> (T) and its maximum value increase. In the magneto-optical recording temperature range, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> was small enough in all compositions to permit recording, but the magnetization values would vary with the Co concentration. Changes in the temperature dependence of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> indicated that a small amount of Co would cause a transfer from T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> recording to T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">comp</inf> recording.

articleTitle: Effect of High Permeability Film in Magneto-optic Readout Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A readout head combining a high-permeability film and a readout film was fabricated, and the effects of the high-permeability film were studied. Inclusion of the high-permeability film produces a steep increase in the variation of magnetic domain width with respect to the external magnetic field. The magnetic garnet film with the larger change in domain width without the high-permeability film had a similarly larger response with the film. When the magnetic domain width variation was greater than half the spot diameter, saturation occurred at a readout signal level of around 75dB.

articleTitle: High Remanence in Laminated TbFe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Single- and multi-layer high saturation magnetization TbFe films with high rectangularity were studied to obtain a film with high remanence. Lamination resulted in greatly improved remanence. No significant variation in M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is observed in single-layer and double-layer films, but the remanence ratio for films of three layers or more is almost one and the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> increases significantly. At three layers M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> becomes 300 G, a very high value compared with single-layer films. Though K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> decreases monotonically with increase in lamination and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> = 2K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub>/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> decreases too, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub> increases resulting in high remanence.

articleTitle: Optical Magnetic Field Sensors Using Mixed Rare-Earth Iron Garnet Crystals
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Optical magnetic field (current) sensors have recently reached practical application. This paper reports on evaluations of LPE garnet (TbY) IG crystals for magnetic field sensors, and on their optical characteristics. 100 μm thick films were produced on {111} GGG substrate, but pits appeared even when using a Pb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>/B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> melt with a low 6.0 molar ratio. We studied the sensitivity and linearity of the Faraday rotation of these LPE films.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Extraordinary Oscillation of Potential Transformers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A simulation model of extraordinary oscillation in potential transformers (PT) was studied to determine conditions for its occurrence and countermeasures. The extraordinary oscillation is analyzed by solving the simultaneous equations derived from the circuit state equation by the harmonic balance method. Addition of a damping circuit on the PT side, or of a ground compensating capacitance on the system side, are suggested countermeasures, but the analysis results indicate that it is possible to introduce a rational setting method.

articleTitle: Output Characteristics of a Four-Pole Parametric Induction Motor Affected by the Size of Common Magnetic Circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between the width of the common magnetic circuits in a four-pole parametric induction motor and the motor's characteristics was studied. It was found that the smaller the width of the common magnetic circuits the better the motor characteristics are. This seems to be due to the fact that the oscillation stability increases and the effective flux to the rotor increases as the common magnetic circuit width decreases.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of Sputtered Garnet Films by Laser Diode
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Laser diode (LD) recording using magneto-optic films with an attached reflective film was investigated. It was found that recording sensitivity improves as media thickness decreases, suggesting that the sensitivity is determined by the reflective film optical absorption and the thermal capacity of reflective film and media combined. It was concluded that LD recording is possible using sputter garnet film with its excellent opto-magnetic characteristics and stability and has now become realistic.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction Constants of High Bs CoZr Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of small amounts of Zr in CoZr films is discussed. It was found that a Zr concentration of 4 at% or less caused the magnetostriction constant to decrease to 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>. The magnetostriction constant was measured by making one edge of the film stationary, applying a 20 Oe magnetic field in the easy and hard axis directions and measuring the displacement of the free edges. The magnetorestriction constant of films with a Zr concentration of 4.8 at% and with various film thickness was nearly constant (it was somewhat smaller for thinner films), but after heat treatment this constant decreased without saturating. The value decreased with decreases in the Zr concentration. The magnetostriction constant of CoZr films with a Zr concentration of 3.4 ~ 4 at% decreased to approximately 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>.

articleTitle: Iron-Oxygen Based Perpendicular Anisotropy Thin Films (Part 1)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetostatic properties of sputtered Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</inf> films with Si or Co added are reported. Si or Co acts to extend the range of perpendicular magnetization to regions of higher magnetization. In the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</inf> system, a point of zero magnetization exists near x = 49%; this is abruptly shifted to lower Fe concentrations with the addition of Si. The observed dependence of magnetization on composition agrees with calculations which assume that silicon combines to form SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and the remaining oxygen forms FeO.

articleTitle: Improvement of Bubble Propagation at Conductor Crossing
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The deterioration of characteristics of bubble propagation in Permalloy film at conductor pattern crossings is investigated, and means for improving propagation studied. Visual observation indicated that bubbles are trapped at crossings; conceivable reasons include 1) conductor pattern strain, 2) magnetic poles generated at steps in the Permalloy, and 3) changes in magnetization characteristics of the Permalloy. Experiments in which conductor patterns were etched away indicated that reason 3), changes in Permalloy characteristics enhanced at step regions, is responsible for the undesired bubble behavior.

articleTitle: Orthorhombic Magnetic Anisotropy in (EuBi)3Fe5O12 Garnet (110) Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It was found that a large orthorhombic anisotropy is induced in (EuBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> garnet films grown on (110) NdGG substrates. The Bi content is controlled by regulating the melt composition and the supercooling temperature. Gyorgy's parameter B = -2(Ku + K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>) increases linearly with the Bi content. The main part of B was found to be growth-induced. Gyorgy's parameter A = K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> - K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> is very small and almost independent of the Bi content. The growth- and stress-induced parts of A were found to be considerably larger, but of opposite sign, and were found to compensate each other almost completely, although their respective absolute values increased with increasing Bi content. The following were obtained as the magnetic properties of the (Eu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1·8</sub> Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1·2</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> film: saturation magnetization 4<o;Ms = 1560 G, uniaxial anisotropy K<sub sub="" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> = 1.6 × 10<sup>5</sup> erg/cm<sup>3</sup>, in-plane anisotropy K<sub>p</sub> = 1.6 × 10<sup>5</sup> erg/cm<sup>3</sup>, quality factor Q = 1.7, material length l = 0.06 μm and wall mobility μw γ<sub>o</sub> = 19 ms<sup>-1</sup>Oe<sup>-1</sup>. Such film might be useful as 0.5-μm bubble material for current access devices.</sub>

articleTitle: Single Pole Type Heads with Co-Zr-Nb/SiO2 Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multilayer films, consisting of two Co-Zr-Nb layers separated by an intermediate SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer were fabricated, and then compared with single-layer films for use in single-pole perpendicular magnetic recording heads. The dependences of film coercivities on the intermediate layer thickness were determined, and domain structures observed. Whereas narrower track widths lead to prominent closure domain effects in single-layer films, unless the anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> is raised, multilayer films with low H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> and an intermediate layer as thin as 30 Å may be used even in narrow-track heads without any drop or instability in playback output.

articleTitle: Ferromagnetic Resonance of Amorphous GdEuCo Alloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: GdEuCo films were made by RF sputtering with magnetic fields that were either parallel or perpendicular to the film surface. These samples were rotated at right angles to the magnetic field to study the angle dependence of the spin wave resonance. Ferromagnetic resonance measurements were performed in the 9 GHz band at both room and liquid-nitrogen temperatures. H⊥ increased gradually with the Eu concentration up to 10 at% where it dropped suddenly. Spin wave resonance was observed for all Eu concentrations (0 ~ 10 at%).

articleTitle: Development of a Lung Magnetic Field Measurement Car
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Development of a mobile lung field measurement system using the very high sensitivity SQUID fluxmeter based on superconduction technology, which enables the measurement of minute magnetic fields, is described. Previous systems could only be moved by dismantling them, making it difficult to put them in locations with low magnetic noise. This system makes it possible to measure the quantity of dust accumulated in the lung, which cannot be detected by x-rays.

articleTitle: Process of Magnetization Reversal in a Spot Heated by Pulsed Laser Beam
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A pulsed laser beam was fired at Tb(FeCo) films (2 μm spot diameter) and its effect on Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) aging was studied, using an avalanche photo diode (APD) as a monitor. It was found that in RE-rich films, the magnetization changed whether or not a bias magnetic field was applied. No such signal was observed in TM-rich films in zero magnetic fields, possibly because of the formation of alternating maze domains within the laser spot which cancel out the Kerr rotation angle.

articleTitle: Transverse Fluxes and Magnetic Characteristics of Three-Phase Transformer Core with Ducts
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The influence of the perpendicular ducts in a three-phase transformer core on the magnetic characteristics is studied by using the finite element method. The relationship between the duct width and the flux distribution are examined in detail. It is clarified that the transverse flux at the duct cannot be ignored.

articleTitle: Coal Powder Beneficiation by Dry Hgms Process--American Coal
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for the beneficiation of American coal powder without using a liquid dispersion medium was investigated. In this method the coal powder is fluidized in a high gradient magnetic field region. Processing American coal by this technique resulted in a performance level yield of 80 percent and ash reduction rate of 30 percent, which were rather good results. Also, no reduction in separation efficiency was observed when the processing space was drastically increased, so this process presents no serious obstacles to practical applications.

articleTitle: Galvanomagnetic Effect of Amorphous Co-Metal Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The galvanomagnetic effect of Co-metal (Ti, Zr, Nb, or Y) films is discussed. In the 30 ~ 50 at% range, the metal element always lost its ferromagnetic characteristics, and γH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> had a corresponding tendency to become zero. R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>/&3x003C1; and ρ are proportional regardless of the metal element used, indicating that a quantum mechanical side jump mechanism causes this anomalous Hall effect. The Δρ/ρ composition dependence, however, changes qualitatively with the type of metal used. When Ti, Zr, or Nb is increased, Δρ/ρ displays an abrupt initial decrease, and reaches a minimum below zero. Both Δρ/ρ and the magnetization become zero at approximately the same composition. There was no change of sign for Y.

articleTitle: Substrate Bias Voltage Effect on Properties of TbCo Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of substrate voltage on TbCo amorphous films is discussed. Changes in the saturation magnetization (M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy constant (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>) were measured while varying the substrate bias voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>). The substrates were coated with Cr, which stabilized the bias voltage between target and substrate resulting in the reproducible film properties. Without Cr coating, M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> did not vary in a consistent manner, and most films tested had perpendicular and in-plane components. Varying electric potential and sputtering electrical discharge may have caused this inconsistency.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Co-Cr Films by CMF Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co-Cr films were prepared by CMF magnetron sputtering, and the effects of the background pressure P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bg</inf> on the film structure and magnetic properties were investigated. When P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bg</inf> was sufficiently low, films had a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and satisfactory characteristics; but the perpendicular orientation deteriorated rapidly as P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bg</inf> was increased above 0.1 mPa, and the coercivity and anisotropy field likewise decreased. These results agree in part with previous results for films formed by rf diode sputtering.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Properties of Double Layer Perpendicular Rigid Disks
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Perpendicular magnetic recording is a promising method for the achievement of higher recording densities. The magnetic and crystal orientational properties of double-layer rigid disks for perpendicular magnetic recording were studied. The coercive force distribution in the Mo-Cu-Permalloy underlayer was investigated as a function of the sputtering gas pressure. At optimum Ar gas pressure, good uniformity of the coercive force distribution was obtained. Even in double-layer media, the crystal orientation of the Co-Cr layer is influenced by the characteristics and thickness of the treated surface layer of the substrate. Higher recording densities were obtained using a lower flying height and a thinner Co-Cr layer. A D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> recording density of 70 kFRPI was achieved for a 0.15-μm Co-Cr layer and a 0.3 μm thick singlepole type head at a flying height of 0.1 μm.

articleTitle: Horizontal Incidence Observation of Magnetic Fields in the Scanning Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for observing the leakage magnetic fields from recorded bits in magnetic media samples is described. When a primary electron beam is directed parallel to the surface of the sample, the Lorentz force resulting from the leakage field deflects electrons either toward or away from the sample surface; those deflected toward the sample strike the surface, generating secondary electrons. By scanning the surface with such a beam, secondary electron images showing the contrast of the magnetic leakage field may be obtained. It is shown that the images thus obtained are different for samples with perpendicular and with in-plane magnetization.

articleTitle: Microscopic Structure and Magnetic Properties of Bi Added FeMn Alloy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic thin films of Mn-ferrite (MnFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) have shown a large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy by the evaporation method. The evaporation substances are the (AαBß)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> system, where A, B, and C represent the matrix elements of combination for Mn, Fe, and Bi, respectively. For (Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">97</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, column-shaped MnFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> grains deposited on a substrate have an anisotropy constant of 4.4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of 1.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> G, and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of 540 Oe. The structure and magnetic properties of such evaporated films are closely related. It was recognized that in order to obtain magnetic thin films with perpendicular anisotropy, it is important to form a first Bi-phase layer with ≪102≫ orientation on the substrate.

articleTitle: Preparation of Bi, Ga-substituted Garnet Films on Glass Substrates by RF Sputtering I
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of ion substitution at rare earth sites and iron sites in garnet was studied to reduce crystallization temperature. Films formed using a Bi, Ga-substituted YIG target on various types of glass substrate were amorphous at low substrate temperatures. Crystallization occurred at around 660°C for a Bi-substitution amount in the range 1.2 to 1.4, but combining Bi-substitution amount over 2 and Ga-substitution enabled reduction of crystallization temperature to around 520°C, though high Bi substitution makes the garnet phase unstable.

articleTitle: Embryonic Development of Frogs Under ELF Magnetic or Electric Fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of extremely low frequency (ELF) magnetic and electric fields on the initial embryonic development of frogs was studied. The embryos were destroyed by a 20 Hz ac current applied directly to the embryos for eight hours in the cleavage-blastula stage as the current density exceeded 100 μA/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. When applied to the embryos in the cleavage-blastra stage, embryo development was disturbed when mRNA synthesis began, and subsequently embryo development was generally abnormal. Thus, electromagnetic fields exert a powerful influence on embryo development in the latter half of the cleavage stage.

articleTitle: Preparation of Bi, Ga-substituted Garnet Films on Glass Substrates by RF Sputtering II
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between film growth, heat treatment conditions, optical heterogeneities, and grain boundaries was studied in Bi, Ga-substituted YIG films. Films formed in an Ar atmosphere and heat treated for 3 hours at 540°C in O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> was optically very homogeneous but slightly magnetically inhomogeneous. In spite of these magnetic inhomegeneities, the written bits were almost perfect circles and distortion was insignificant.

articleTitle: Effects of Additive Gases on Properties of Co-Cr Film Media During High Rate Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of the introduction of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> during high-rate sputtering on the magnetic properties of resulting Co-Cr film were studied. O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> react with the Co-Cr to form compounds. Addition of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> induces an fcc ≪200≫ orientation perpendicular to the film plane, thereby causing a drastic decrease in the perpendicular anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>, accompanied by degradation in the hcp ≪002≫ orientation. O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is the most reactive with Co-Cr, but has little effect on the crystal structure. These effects are diminished at higher deposition rates for the same gas pressure. In contrast, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> does not react with Co-Cr at all, but plays a unique role in that it changes the coercive force without any accompanying change in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> or the crystal orientation. The effects of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are concluded to be equivalent, respectively, to the effects of raising and of lowering the substrate temperature.

articleTitle: Possible Mechanism of Mode Change to Vertical Magnetization from In-Plane Magnetization in TbCo Layered Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Formulas are presented for calculating the energy of an antiferromagnetic body to clarify the mechanism of change from vertical to in-plane magnetization in TbCo layered films. The formulas are based on the assumptions that the bias current used in forming the layered film includes short-period pulsation current, resulting in the formation of an amorphous-state epitaxial natural lattice; and that each of the layers of the TbCo film consists of two-dimensional lattices.

articleTitle: Ion Beam Sputtered Films of Bismuth-Substituted Yttrium Iron Garnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Compared with the conventional liquid phase epitaxy method (LPE), ion beam sputtering (IBS) has advantages in heavy doping of Bi ions, since it is an essentially nonthermal equilibrium process. IBS was used to prepare Bi-substituted YIG films. Epitaxial growth along the {111} direction was observed, however, and small amounts of polycrystalline garnet phase were also found. Bi content of the films reached 2.75/(formula unit). Investigation of the dependences of Faraday rotation on Bi content of the films and on the target composition showed that Faraday rotation reached a maximum of -4.3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> deg/cm, as high as that reported for LPE grown films [1]. Slight contamination of the films by the materials of the ion gun, the grids, iris, wall and target holder was detected.

articleTitle: Magnetism of Rapidly Quenched Amorphous Fe-Sm Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structural analysis and investigation of magnetic properties were carried out on rapidly quenched Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub> Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> (10.5 ≤ × ≤ 80) alloys. Amorphous alloys were fabricated in a wide composition range from x = 17 to 72.5. The composition dependence of Curie temperature and magnetization was found to be similar to that of amorphous Fe-(Nd, Pr) alloys and could be considered to be caused by the change in short-range atomic order with Sm concentration. A maximum coercive force of about 1.1 kOe at 300 K and 12 kOe at 77 K is obtained in x = 40 alloy. The rapid decrease in coercive force on raising temperature can be explained by the wall pinning model proposed by Gaunt. After heating the amorphous alloys up to 900 K, they transform into metastable Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> Sm (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 465 K) + α - Fe (x < 20), unknown metastable phase (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 555 K) + α - Fe (20 ≤ × ≤ 33.3) and Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> Sm (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 670 K) + Sm (x ≥ 40).

articleTitle: Structure and Perpendicular Magnetic Properties of FeBi Films by Evaporation Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Media for use in perpendicular magnetic recording must have a magnetic anisotropy directed normal to the film surface; as recording densities continue to rise, this method is fast becoming a center of attention. In a previous report, we focused on magnetic thin films with a perpendicular anisotropy caused by the shape anisotropy due to nonmagnetic impurities in films, the orientation of the film crystal and a columnar microstructure, and reported on the magnetic properties of (FeMn)Bi system thin films. In connection with this, we studied the magnetic properties and structure of FeBi thin films, and found that slight changes in the Bi concentration had a profound effect on the growth of crystal grains, with corresponding changes in the magnetization and coercivity of the evaporated ffilms. When columnar grains form in the Fe (110) direction, normal to the substrate, as occurs in 3000 Å thick films with a Bi concentration of 1.6 at% and grown at a substrate temperature of approx. 100°C, perpendicular magnetization film with a coercivity of 500 Oe and a remanent magnetization of 630 G is obtained.

articleTitle: Galvanomagnetic Effects in Sm-Co Amorphous Magnetic Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The galvanomagnetic effects of SmCo amorphous magnetic films are discussed. In films with in-plane magnetization, resistivity rose gradually with the Sm concentration, while the Hall resistivity, Hall sensitivity, and Hall voltage peaked around 15 atm% Sm and gradually declined. In perpendicular magnetization films, both the Hall resistivity and Hall sensitivity decreased as the Sm content increased. In both perpendicular and in-plane magnetization film, the Kerr rotation angle decreased as the Sm concentration increased.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Ion Beam Sputtered CoCrTa Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To suppress segregation in CoCr film for use in rigid disk media, the authors studied the properties of ion beam sputtered CoCr thin films with Ta added, formed at different substrate temperatures and to different film thicknesses. Films retain a high H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> at low Ta contents (≪ 3 at%), and films of thicknesses 0.1 μm and below showed a perpendicular orientation. As little segregation occurs in such films, they are regarded as suitable for use in perpendicular recording media.

articleTitle: Stress Sensitive Property of Fe-base Amorphous Alloy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The high stress sensitivity of Fe-base amorphous alloy was studied. Permeability variation under uniaxial tensile stress measurements showed that the alloy had a saturation magnetostriction of 20 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> and a Young's modulus of 10000 kg/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Permeability variation reached maximum in the neighborhood of 20 kHz, exhibiting the same tendency when the level was varied from 20 to 100 mOe. These results confirm the previous result that magnetization conditions of 20 kHz and 20 mOe are appropriate when making use of stress sensitivity.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Magnetoresistive Element Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of performing annealing in a magnetic field after magneto resistive (MR) element formation in yoke-type MR heads were studied. It was found that the annealing temperature range in which an amorphous alloy with high permeability is obtained was close to 440-450°C. The fine stripe MR element formed before the amorphous alloy film is affected by annealing in a magnetic field. At a film thickness of 300 Å, as annealing temperature increased, anisotropy was dispersed. The experiment demonstrated conclusively that it is possible to realize high-permeability amorphous alloy film yoke-type MR heads.

articleTitle: Finite Element Method Analysis for Recording Head Under Complex Permeability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The influence of complex permeability on magnetic recording heads was analyzed using strict formulas for the finite element method modified to take account of complex permeability. Positional differences between the field intensity and flux density at each frequency showed that there is a loss coefficient due to complex permeability. This loss coefficient is practically zero at all frequencies in the conventional model.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Effect on Growth of Cucumbers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Experiments on summer cultivation of cucumbers in a magnetic field were conducted to determine the optimum growth conditions using the well-known effects of magnetic fields on germination and growth of vegetables. Seed processing at 5 Oe for 72 hours had remarkable effects. Most of the seeds germinated in 30 hours. However, no appreciable difference was observed between seeds processed at 150 Oe for one hour, and seeds not processed in a magnetic field. Overall, cultivation in a magnetic field after processing in a low magnetic field for a long time provides the most favorable growth conditions.

articleTitle: Aging Changes of Some Properties of Amorphous TbFeAl Thin Films as a Magneto-Optical Recording Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of Al addition on the deterioration of TbFeAl films is discussed. Oxidation of films with no protective layer was observed at temperatures between 100° and 200° C. Variation in the transmittance was attributed to the varying thickness of the oxidation layer. No pinholes were observed. The addition of Al to TbFe film reduces room temperature oxidation by a factor of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>.

articleTitle: Effective Permeability due to High Temperature Annealing in Amorphous Alloy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of heat treatment conditions on the high-frequency characteristics of amorphous materials was studied. In the range 300 kHz to 1 MHz, permeability reached a peak at a heat treatment time of around 100 min., about 20 percent higher than the permeability peak for short duration heat treatment. Permeability increased at 1 MHz for all heat treatment temperatures, peak time decreasing with increase in heat treatment temperature. It was confirmed that it is possible to have both a composition with T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> close to each other, and to use water quenching heat treatment.

articleTitle: Gd-Base Amorphous Magneto-Optical Films with Large Kerr Rotations
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Gd-Fe-Co system has a high Kerr rotation under a forced magnetic field, but this is an in-plane magnetized film. We attempted to produce a perpendicularly magnetized film by adding Tb, Dy or Ho to GdFeCo with high Kerr rotation. Measurement of the variation with temperature of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> for the samples with Tb, Dy and Ho substituted showed that θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> was higher for all of them than for the Tb-Fe-Co over the whole temperature range, indicating that they have a sufficiently large θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> value and that high playback output can be obtained. When static recording was performed on Gd-Dy-Fe-Co perpendicularly magnetized film, excellent recording bit formations of diameter 1.3 μm were obtained.

articleTitle: Orthorhombic Magnetic Anisotropy of {110} GdBi Garnet Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Four series of {110} GdBi garnet film bubble memory media with orthorhombic anisotropy were grown on {110} Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> garnet substrates. The orthorhombic anisotropy energy differences K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> ([110] to [001]) and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> ([110] to [110]) were calculated from the anisotropic magnetic field and the 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> value. Values were thus obtained for parameters A and B in Gyorgy's two-parameter model. Calculations of the growth-induced component of the Gyorgy parameters A and B as functions of growth temperature showed that, in the fourth series of films, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</sup> and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sup> were identical.
