Up to now, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</sup> and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sup> have the same values only for (YBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (FeGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>. 3 μm-diameter bubble material was obtained using the third series of films.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Analysis in Buried Pipe Detection
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Mangetic detection is known as a useful method to detect the position of a buried pipe. The detection, however, becomes erroneous except in the case of a single pipe-line. We have considered a case of two pipe-lines running parallel each other to gain a theoretical understanding of the error cause, and compared the results analyzed to those experimentally measured. Both results are in good agreement. The error is due to an earth current leaking from a considered line toward another line nearby.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Co-Based Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of heat treatment on the magnetostriction constants and film stress of CoZr and CoZrTa films was studied. Heat treatment decreased positive magnetostriction constants, while increasing negative magnetostriction constants. Also it was learned that heat treatment converts the compression stress of sputtering into tensile stress. The authors attribute magnetic structural changes to magnetic elastic energy and point out that the magnetostriction constants and film stress are as important in these films as they are in Permalloy films.

articleTitle: High Frequency Characteristics of a Magnetic Coaxial Pipe Made of Amorphous Ribbons
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization, impedance, and other characteristics of magnetic coaxial pipe formed by winding amorphous ribbons is reported. Amorphous ribbons, with Cu foil on either edge, were wound into toroids, with leads soldered to the Cu. The impedance of the inner pipe was found to be several hundred times that of the outer pipe when driven at a frequency of 100 kHz, greater than for Permalloy pipes driven at 50 Hz. Such nonuniform radial distributions of permeability and current density may enable applications as unique circuit elements.

articleTitle: Effect of Nonuniform Flux Distribution on Iron Loss in Amorphous Toroidal Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Nonuniform flux distributions in amorphous toroidal cores can result in anomalous eddy current losses. Amorphous toroidal cores were excited (by a sinusoidal magnetic flux) and the resulting core losses and local flux distributions measured. Though the overall core flux was sinusoidal, the local flux distribution was distorted, and the distortion is thought to cause the 1.5 times greater eddy current loss than for sinusoidal flux at 50 Hz. This would explain the large anomaly factor in part using Pry and Bean's model, assuming domain widths in agreement with measured values.

articleTitle: Generation and Propagation of Magnetoelastic wave in Amorphous Wire
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetoelastic wave propagation in amorphous wire was observed. The dependence of the attenuation constant on the magnetic field was determined by applying a dc field to the propagation path. Comparison with results obtained for amorphous ribbons showed that despite the measurement made at a higher frequency, the attenuation constant for the wire at high fields was lower, confirming that measurements can be made for wires at higher frequencies than for ribbons.

articleTitle: Reproducing Analysis of Hybrid Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Read-out characteristics of a compound type head with excellent recording characteristics were studied. It was found that the magnetization gradient and residual magnetization both decreased as the depth of the media increased, and that the requirements of permeability and saturation flux density for low-saturation flux density films are not hard to satisfy. With its low-saturation flux density layer, read-out characteristics in this compound head were as good as those in other types of heads.

articleTitle: Noncontact Mechanocardiograph Sensor Using an Amorphous-Coro Multivibrator
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An experimental noncontact mechanocardiograph sensor was made using an amorphous-core multivibrator sensor to improve the operation of instruments. The 0 to 120 Hz components were detected by the amorphous sensor and sensitivity was high. By comparison, the Apex cordis beat (0 to 5 Hz) was not detected by the conventional acceleration transducer and detection sensitivity for the 30 to 60 Hz components was low. It was also found that distinction between noise patterns, phonocardiograph signal to noise ratio and other features were much better using the amorphous sensor than when the conventional acceleration transducer was used.

articleTitle: Stochastic Boundary Element Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic field analysis using the stochastic finite element method makes prohibitive demands on computer memory and processing capacity. The authors propose a new approach, based on boundary element techniques, which, as with finite element methods, requires partitioning sufficiently fine to enable tracing of the auto-correlation function, but without requiring as much computer memory for execution.

articleTitle: Dependence of Magnetic Properties of Metal Evaporated Tape on O2 Gas Flow Rate
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co-Ni films were evaporated on PET substrates with oxygen gas introduced into the chamber at various flow rates (0 ~ 300 ml), and its effects on the magnetic properties of the films were studied with its flow rate as a parameter. From the angular distribution of the film coercivity, two switching mechanisms seemed to exist in the film. They are 1) coherent rotation of the magnetization, and 2) domain wall motion. At higher O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow rates the former region tended to broaden, suggesting a finer columnar grain structure. The dependence of coercivities on temperature grew more marked at higher oxygen flow rates.

articleTitle: Analysis of 3D Magnetic Fields in Wiggler Magnets for Free-Electron Laser
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: To obtain the desired magnetic flux density distribution, the authors studied modifications of wiggler magnets for use in free electron lasers. The effects of magnet positions and the magnetization within magnets on the flux density distribution in two dimensions in the cavity between magnets were clarified. A three-dimensional finite element method was used to calculate distributions, and good qualitative agreement obtained with experiments using ferrite plastic magnets.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Thermal Stability of Co-(Nb,Ta)-Zr
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structural changes and heat stability of the soft magnetic characteristics of Co-(Nb,Ta)-Zr films are discussed. Following annealing, both samples exhibited extremely high levels of thermal stability, with the characteristics of CoNbZrTa films slightly better than those of CoNbZr films. The results of electron beam diffraction showed that the films have a very regular structure which is virtually unaffected by heat treatment. Experimental results also suggested that changes in the soft magnetic characteristics of such films are due to structural changes, and the high thermal stability is due to the lower speed of these changes.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Co-Cr Films with Large Perpedicular Anisotropy by Using a Roll-Coater Sputtering System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The crystal orientation and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Co-Cr films, sputtered in such a manner that a composition gradient exists in the depth direction, were studied. By making the initially deposited layer Cr-rich compared to material subsequently deposited on the substrate, which is in constant motion relative to the target, an effect equivalent to a base layer controlling the film crystal orientation was achieved. Compared with films of uniform composition, improved perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and crystal orientation were realized.

articleTitle: Co-Ferrite Films By Thermal Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co-ferrite film was fabricated by the thermal decomposition method and its various characteristics were determined. M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> variation agreed with that of the film X-ray diffraction peak intensity suggesting that it corresponds to the degree of crystallization. The crystal grains of the film were found to be small with diameters in the range 1000 to 2000 Å, apparently one cause of the high H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. It was confirmed that Co-ferrite film fabricated by the thermal decomposition method has excellent characteristics for use as opto-magnetic recording material.

articleTitle: Two Step Jumps in Core-Type Nonlinear Zero-Phase-Sequence Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic frequency multipliers employing core-type zero-phase-sequence circuits boast high conversion efficiencies and other advantages, but the asymmetric circuit configuration gives rise to a two-jump phenomenon in the I/O characteristics for light loads. An analysis was conducted employing harmonic balance methods, and taking into account the asymmetry of the problem; calculated results agreed well with experiments in indicating the presence of the "jump" in the operating characteristics. The effects of circuit parameters in suppressing this behavior are currently being studied.

articleTitle: Large Barkhausen Effect and Matteucci Effect in Amorphous Magnetostrictive Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The large Barkhausen effect and Matteucci effect generation mechanism in amorphous magnetostrictive wire were studied. It was found that induced magnetic anisotropy perpendicular to the surface of the as-prepared wire is changed into in-plane induced anisotropy along the direction of the tensile force by twisting the wire. Measurement of variation in Matteucci voltage e'<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> with twisting revealed that the magnetization vector changed from the irregular directions to a uniform direction along the twisting, indicating that e'<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> increases greatly with respect to twisting stress.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-C Films Prepared by Getter Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties and structure of Fe-C system thin films were studied. Values of the intrinsic coercivity <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> increase from 50 ~ 70 Oe at a substrate temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> = 200°C to their maxima of 250 ~ 310 Oe at T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> = 350°C. The saturation magnetization M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> varies from 600 to 900 G, reaching a minima in the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> range between 300 to 400°C, where the <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> values are maxima. X-ray diffraction analyses show an amorphous structure for the film at T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> = 150°C, and show several peaks for those at T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</inf> = 250 ~ 400°C indicating micro-crystals of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C, Fe and C.

articleTitle: Bias Magnetic Field Dependence of RF Permeability in Thin Permalloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dependence of RF permeability (μRF = μ'RF - j μ''RF) on a bias magnetic field (H: corresponding to a signal field) in a permalloy film, when H and RF exciting magnetic fields (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RF</sub>) are in the direction of the hard axis in Permalloy films, was analyzed with the film taken as a single domain, the demagnetizing field in the film plane taken as 0, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RF</sub> assumed to be sufficiently small compared with the anisotropic field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>, and H assumed to be static. It was found that the μ'RF change is sharp at ω < ωK (ωß: ferromagnetic resonance frequency at H = 0) and the μ''RF change is sharp at ω ≃ ωK.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of SmCo Sputter-Deposited Polycrystalline Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: SmCo polycrystalline films were sputter-formed on glass substrates at temperatures between 200 and 300°C, and relations between precipitated phases and film magnetic properties were studied. Phases with Sm-Co stoichiometric ratios of 2-17, 1-5, 1-3, and 1-2 were tentatively identified; these phases exhibit widely varying coercivities, in the ranges of several hundred Oe, several kOe, around 10 kOe, and under 100 Oe, respectively. Except SmCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, all other phases, which were of hexagonal structure, resulted in a large negative K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> value for the film.

articleTitle: Simulation Model for Perpendicular Co-Cr Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Potter-Beardsley model is used to calculate the Co-Cr perpendicular magnetic film magnetization to investigate the influence of the model parameters. A magnetization curve in the perpendicular direction on the media surface was different from the curve obtained experimentally by Iwasaki. It was demonstrated that the experimental results could be explained by modifying the Potter-Beardsley model to take account of the exchange coupling magnetic field.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability and Reliability of Magneto-Optical Media with Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Using a constant power source and both binary and single target magnetron sputtering, samples with periodic structures were produced while varying the substrate rotation speed. Characteristics reached a maximum at 5 rpm and in-plane magnetization films resulted at 1 rpm. Annealing samples with a protective layer causes all characteristics except the Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) to vary. These variations were peculiar to periodic structures. The change in the coercive force (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) indicated a structural transition. The large H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and saturation magnetization (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) values promise superior recording resolution. The carrier-to-noise ratio was improved by one to two dB and showed no changes after 1000 h in the open air at 55°C.

articleTitle: Reducing Treatment Effects on Absorption Loss in (BiGdCa)3(FeAlGa)5O12 Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The absorption loss of (BiGdCa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(FeAlGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> films is discussed. In the films grown at a growth temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>) in the range 745 to 764°C, the absorption loss was 1 ~ 3 dB/cm. It was conjectured that the increase in the absorption loss of the films grown below T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> = 740°C was due mainly to film defects. Absorption loss for this Bi-substituted garnet film was almost equal to that for reduction treated Ca:YIG with low impurity density at λ = 1.15 μm, but at λ = 0.79 μm the Bi-substituted garnet film absorption loss was 220 dB/cm and it was almost twice that of the Ca:YIG film. The increase in absorption loss at 0.79 μm seems to be due to the fact that when Bi and Pb are substituted, the absorption edge for the film shifts to longer wavelengths and extends as far as the 0.79 μm wavelength.

articleTitle: A Novel Detection Method of Flux Level in a Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new method for detecting the flux level in a magnetic core is proposed, which enables the use of artificial two-phase amplitude detection to improve the response time. Two cores are employed, with operating points set deep within the range of saturation to raise detection sensitivity and eliminate hysteresis effects, and a response time equivalent to one quarter-cycle of the driving voltage frequency was achieved.

articleTitle: Preparation of GdIG:Bi Single Crystals by Crucible Rotation Flux Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: GdIG single crystals with Bi substituted were grown by the crucible rotation flux method to reduce the optical absorption loss in the near infrared range. This loss is a serious problem with rare earth iron garnets used for optical isolators. The grown crystals have extremely few carriers, and the resistances are in the range 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> Ω-cm as compared with 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Ω-cm for crystals prepared by the conventional technique. It is thought that the oxygen defects, ie, amount of resultant Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, in the GdIG:Bi single crystals grown by this method will be significantly lower than that in similar crystals prepared by the conventional method. The optical absorption loss was one third that of the optical loss in crystals grown by the conventional flux method.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability Measurement of Amorphous Ribbons by High-Sensitive AC-Calorimeter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A highly sensitive AC-calorimeter which measures the specific heat changes of amorphous ribbons during heat treatment was devised. Using the results of these measurements, the structural relaxation and recrystallization processes of such ribbons were very closely examined. Using this method, the onset of structural relaxation, recrystallization and even magnetic phase transition was detected from large increases or peaks in the specific heat of the samples. Samples were also examined at different temperatures using X-ray diffraction to determine their structural properties.

articleTitle: Columnar Structure in Continuously Sputtered Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co-Cr films were continuously formed on a substrate film in motion by DC planar magnetron sputtering, and the effect on the columnar microstructure of films was investigated. Columnar grains were bow-shaped owing to the change in angle of incidence ø of sputtered particles, in contrast with films formed on a stationary substrate; but the extent of change in ø had little effect. These results can be approximated using a vector sum representing sputtering from two line sources.

articleTitle: Planar-Type Micro-Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of planar-type micro-magnetic cores, consisting of pairs of (primary and secondary) plane coils and Co-Fe amorphous magnetic ribbons in different configurations, are reported. The output was measured for sinusoidal exciting currents at different frequencies in different coils; results differed depending on whether an amorphous ribbon was inserted between coil pairs, and on the pitch between coils. Experimental results agreed well with calculations of the flux density distribution in the coil thickness direction, equivalent to the linkage flux.

articleTitle: Dependence on Sputtering Conditions for a Tb-Co Magneto-Optical Thin Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: TbCo films were prepared by simultaneous magnetron Co-sputtering. The influences of the sputtering conditions on the density and magneto-optical properties were studied. Sputtering conditions such as substrate rotating speed, substrate bias voltage, Ar pressure, and film deposition rate were studied. Increasing the bias voltage or Ar pressure decreased the density of the TbCo film. This indicates that the incident energy and/or density of Ar ions and/or atoms affect the porosity of the film. This could be closely related to the magneto-optical properties of the film.

articleTitle: Sputter Preparation of Mn-Zn Ferrite Thin Film with Soft Magnetic Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An Mn-Zn ferrite (111) surface oriented film was fabricated on an amorphous Mn-Zn ferrite (a-MZ) layer as a backing layer for a Ba-ferrite media to investigate the problem of diffusion of Zn ions from the the ZnO layer to the Mn-Zn ferrite layer. X-ray diffraction revealed that the experiment samples had almost perfect (111) surface orientation and that this degree of orientation is strongly dependent on the foundation a-MZ layer film thickness δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>, with δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> ≃ 100 Å giving the most favorable orientation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Saturation in Perpendicular Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Results of investigations involving calculations using the finite element method and experiments to determine the magnetic saturation during writing for both closed-circuit configuration single-sided heads and open-circuit configuration separated type heads are reported. The single-sided head reaches the same magnetic flux density as the separated-type head at approximately 1/3 the recording current, and the single-sided head has almost three times the recording efficiency of the separated-type head. In the single-sided head magnetic flux density within the media is restricted by magnetic saturation within the closed magnetic circuit.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Magnetoresistive Element Annealed in Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetoresistive (MR) effect and anisotropy field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> in NiFe thin films, annealed in dc and rotating magnetic fields, were studied. In large MR elements, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> decreased with annealing at temperatures up to 300°C due to stress relaxation. When the annealing temperature exceeded 350°C, the Δ&3x003C1;/ρ vs. H curves measured along both the hard and easy axes of magnetization showed a large dispersive hysteresis. This resulted in a decrease in Δρ/Δ. In MR elements consisting of a narrow stripe, on the other hand, the magnetoresistive and magnetic properties of the NiFe film changed hardly at all for temperatures up to 500°C, because they were controlled by the shape magnetic anisotropy. An MR head with a magnetic yoke consisting of amorphous CoNbZr was fabricated. The MR head was annealed in dc and rotating magnetic fields in order to obtain a high yoke permeability. A satisfactory MR characteristic was attained for the NiFe film in the head.

articleTitle: Study on the Magnetically Soft Materials of Si-Added Low Ni Permalloy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Si was added to high-permeability Ni-Fe permalloy with approximately 38% Ni to increase the ac magnetic characteristics and the effects on the magnetic properties and resistivity were investigated. It was found H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is improved, but the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> characteristics were worse for samples annealed at 1300°C. The effective permeability μe of samples annealed at 1000°C and at 1200°C showed a similar tendency to decrease over the measured frequency range of 1 kHz to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical and Magnetic Properties of Co-Substituted BaM
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: BaM(BaFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sub>) has strong crystal anisotropy, but its Faraday rotation is low at only 0.22 deg/μm (λ= 780 nm). An attempt to improve the properties of this material as magneto-optical recording media by replacing part of the Fe in BaM with Co is discussed. It was found that θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> increased with the amount of Co substituted. The investigation confirmed that Co is effective in increasing BaM θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>. When La is used for Co charge compensation, along with increasing θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>, it was also found that the crystal anisotropy becomes high, and the properties of the material as magneto-optical recording media improved.
